   429	// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   430	// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   431	//
   432	// SubagentTokens is handled differently from the other fields: main-agent
   433	// usage (InputTokens, OutputTokens, ...) arrives per step as a delta scoped to
   434	// that step's transcript slice, so it is correct to sum deltas across steps.
   435	// Subagent usage arrives as a cumulative-since-session-start snapshot instead
   436	// — CalculateTotalTokenUsage discovers agent IDs from the full transcript
   437	// (so a subagent spawned before the current checkpoint window is still
   438	// found) and re-reads each subagent transcript from its start on every call.
   439	// Summing that snapshot across steps would re-add a subagent's full usage on
   440	// every subsequent step after it was first discovered, so SubagentTokens is
   441	// replaced with the latest snapshot rather than added.
   442	func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   443		if incoming == nil {
   444			return existing
   445		}
   446		if existing == nil {
   447			// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   448			return &agent.TokenUsage{
   449				InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   450				CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   451				CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   452				OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   453				APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   454				SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   455			}
   456		}
   457	
   458		// Accumulate values
   459		existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   460		existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   461		existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   462		existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   463		existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   464	
   465		// Replace (not add) subagent tokens: incoming.SubagentTokens is already
   466		// the cumulative total as of this step, so the latest snapshot supersedes
   467		// whatever was recorded before rather than stacking on top of it.
   468		if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   469			existing.SubagentTokens = incoming.SubagentTokens
   470		}

   307	// mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
   308	// All paths are normalized to forward slashes for platform-agnostic storage.
   309	func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
   310		seen := make(map[string]bool)
   311		for _, f := range existing {
   312			seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
   313		}
   314	
   315		for _, list := range fileLists {
   316			for _, f := range list {
   317				seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
   318			}
   319		}
   320	
   321		result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
   322		for f := range seen {
   323			result = append(result, f)
   324		}
   325	
   326		// Sort for deterministic output
   327		sort.Strings(result)
   328		return result
   329	}

   364	func applyTaskRecordCompletion(state *SessionState, rec session.TaskRecord) error {

   429	// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   430	// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   431	//
   432	// SubagentTokens is handled differently from the other fields: main-agent
   433	// usage (InputTokens, OutputTokens, ...) arrives per step as a delta scoped to
   434	// that step's transcript slice, so it is correct to sum deltas across steps.
   435	// Subagent usage arrives as a cumulative-since-session-start snapshot instead
   436	// — CalculateTotalTokenUsage discovers agent IDs from the full transcript
   437	// (so a subagent spawned before the current checkpoint window is still
   438	// found) and re-reads each subagent transcript from its start on every call.
   439	// Summing that snapshot across steps would re-add a subagent's full usage on
   440	// every subsequent step after it was first discovered, so SubagentTokens is
   441	// replaced with the latest snapshot rather than added.
   442	func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   443		if incoming == nil {
   444			return existing
   445		}
   446		if existing == nil {
   447			// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   448			return &agent.TokenUsage{
   449				InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   450				CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   451				CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   452				OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   453				APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   454				SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   455			}
   456		}
   457	
   458		// Accumulate values
   459		existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   460		existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   461		existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   462		existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   463		existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   464	
   465		// Replace (not add) subagent tokens: incoming.SubagentTokens is already
   466		// the cumulative total as of this step, so the latest snapshot supersedes
   467		// whatever was recorded before rather than stacking on top of it.
   468		if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   469			existing.SubagentTokens = incoming.SubagentTokens
   470		}

   307	// mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
   308	// All paths are normalized to forward slashes for platform-agnostic storage.
   309	func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {
   310		seen := make(map[string]bool)
   311		for _, f := range existing {
   312			seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
   313		}
   314	
   315		for _, list := range fileLists {
   316			for _, f := range list {
   317				seen[filepath.ToSlash(f)] = true
   318			}
   319		}
   320	
   321		result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
   322		for f := range seen {
   323			result = append(result, f)
   324		}
   325	
   326		// Sort for deterministic output
   327		sort.Strings(result)

   357	// and to the session: files merge into FilesTouched (invariant: carry-forward

   361	// separate counter.

   363	// overwrites live.Files rather than merging.
   364	func applyTaskRecordCompletion(state *SessionState, rec session.TaskRecord) error {
   365		live := state.FindTaskRecord(rec.ToolUseID)

   429	// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   430	// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   431	//
   432	// SubagentTokens is handled differently from the other fields: main-agent
   433	// usage (InputTokens, OutputTokens, ...) arrives per step as a delta scoped to
   434	// that step's transcript slice, so it is correct to sum deltas across steps.
   435	// Subagent usage arrives as a cumulative-since-session-start snapshot instead
   436	// — CalculateTotalTokenUsage discovers agent IDs from the full transcript
   437	// (so a subagent spawned before the current checkpoint window is still
   438	// found) and re-reads each subagent transcript from its start on every call.
   439	// Summing that snapshot across steps would re-add a subagent's full usage on
   440	// every subsequent step after it was first discovered, so SubagentTokens is
   441	// replaced with the latest snapshot rather than added.
   442	func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   443		if incoming == nil {
   444			return existing
   445		}
   446		if existing == nil {
   447			// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   448			return &agent.TokenUsage{
   449				InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   450				CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   451				CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   452				OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   453				APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   454				SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   455			}
   456		}
   457	
   458		// Accumulate values
   459		existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   460		existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   461		existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   462		existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   463		existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   464	
   465		// Replace (not add) subagent tokens: incoming.SubagentTokens is already
   466		// the cumulative total as of this step, so the latest snapshot supersedes
   467		// whatever was recorded before rather than stacking on top of it.
   468		if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   469			existing.SubagentTokens = incoming.SubagentTokens
   470		}

    74	// Open resolves the checkpoint storage topology and constructs the backing
    75	// store(s). It keeps ref resolution, backend selection, and blob-fetcher wiring
    76	// in one place. The primary is built through the backend registry; with no
    77	// checkpoints config it resolves to the git-branch backend with no mirrors, so
    78	// default behavior is unchanged. When mirrors are configured, the persistent
    79	// store is a fan-out wrapper (reads from primary, best-effort writes to mirrors).
    80	//
    81	// Backend selection is read via settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig, which resolves
    82	// like settings.Load: from the context's worktree root if set, else relative to
    83	// the current working directory — not from repo. Callers opening a repository
    84	// that is not the cwd should wrap ctx with that worktree root (as dispatch does).
    85	// Resolution is fail-soft about settings CONTENT: a missing settings file, a
    86	// whole-file JSON syntax error, or unrelated invalid fields all yield the
    87	// default git-branch backend with no mirrors, preserving default behavior.
    88	//
    89	// It is not fail-soft about which repository this is. A worktree root that will
    90	// not resolve is returned as an error rather than defaulted, because the backend
    91	// choice would then be made for a repo we could not identify — and the settings
    92	// file that names it is the one we failed to find. That failure is unreachable
    93	// from a command in practice: the root pre-run refuses to run at all when the
    94	// worktree root does not resolve. LoadCheckpointsConfig draws the same line.
    95	func Open(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, opts OpenOptions) (*Stores, error) {
    96		refs := resolveOpenRefs(ctx, opts)
    97		env := OpenEnv{Repo: repo, BlobFetcher: opts.BlobFetcher, RefFetcher: opts.RefFetcher, RemoteRefLister: opts.RemoteRefLister, MetadataBranchFetcher: opts.MetadataBranchFetcher, Refs: refs, ReadRemotes: opts.ReadRemotes}

   102		}

   104		primaryType := resolvePrimaryType(cfg)
   105		primary, err := buildPrimary(ctx, env, primaryType, primaryConfig(cfg))
   106		if err != nil {
   107			return nil, err
   108		}
   109		mirrors, err := buildMirrors(ctx, env, cfg, primaryType)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			return nil, err
   112		}
   113		writer := newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)
   114	
   115		// Kind routing: resolve id-keyed reads and backfill writes by the
   116		// checkpoint's format across both git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex
   117		// ID on the branch or a migrated ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo
   118		// handles either format without reconfiguring. Creates still go through
   119		// writer (configured primary + mirrors).
   120		branchStore, refsStore, err := buildKindReadStores(ctx, env, primaryType, primary)
   121		if err != nil {
   122			return nil, err
   123		}

   125		return &Stores{

   127			ephemeral:  newEphemeralStore(repo, refs),

   129		}, nil
   130	}

   132	// buildKindReadStores returns the git-branch and git-refs read stores used for
   133	// id-kind read routing, reusing the already-built primary for whichever kind it
   134	// is and constructing the sibling. A non-branch/refs git-backed primary (not a
   135	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
   136	// yields both freshly built git stores.
   137	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
   138		switch primaryType {
   139		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
   140			branch = primary
   141			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   142		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
   143			refs = primary
   144			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
   145		default:
   146			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
   147				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   148			}
   149		}

   170	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
   171	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
   174	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   175		if err := ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ); err != nil {
   176			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
   177		}
   178		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
   179	}

   181	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
   182	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
   185	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
   186	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
   187	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
   189	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
   190		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
   191			return nil, nil
   192		}
   193		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
   194		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
   195		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
   196			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
   197				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   198			}
   199			if seen[m.Type] {
   200				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
   201			}
   202			seen[m.Type] = true
   203			// Mirrors are best-effort write-only copies whose failures are logged
   204			// and dropped; never pay on-demand ref-fetch network probes for them.
   205			mirrorEnv := env
   206			mirrorEnv.RefFetcher = nil
   207			store, err := build(ctx, mirrorEnv, m.Type, m.Config)
   208			if err != nil {
   209				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   210			}
   211			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
   212		}
   213		return mirrors, nil
   214	}

    12	// PersistentRefs is the committed-metadata ref topology.
    13	type PersistentRefs struct {
    14		Primary plumbing.ReferenceName
    15		Read    plumbing.ReferenceName
    16		Push    []plumbing.ReferenceName
    17	
    18		// localReadOnly pins reads to the local Read ref with no remote-tracking
    19		// tiers at all — set via PrimaryAsLocalRead. Guards (attach's
    20		// local-presence gates) that must answer "would the next LOCAL write see
    21		// this checkpoint?" need it: the ordinary read chain selects per
    22		// checkpoint across local and remote-tracking trees, so a checkpoint
    23		// present only on a remote would otherwise read as present and a write
    24		// based on the stale local branch would clobber the remote on push.
    25		localReadOnly bool
    26	}

    28	// DefaultV1Refs returns the v1-only topology.
    29	func DefaultV1Refs() PersistentRefs {
    30		v1Branch := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
    31		return PersistentRefs{
    32			Primary: v1Branch,
    33			Read:    v1Branch,
    34			Push:    []plumbing.ReferenceName{v1Branch},
    35		}
    36	}

    38	// PrimaryFetchableFromRemote reports whether Primary has a remote-tracking
    39	// shadow on whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    40	// remote-tracking ref).
    41	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() bool {
    42		return r.Primary.IsBranch() && slices.Contains(r.Push, r.Primary)
    43	}
    44

    46	// whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    47	// remote-tracking ref): true when reads target Primary and Primary is
    48	// fetchable from a remote, and the topology was not pinned local-only.
    49	func (r PersistentRefs) ReadBootstrappableFromRemote() bool {
    50		return !r.localReadOnly && r.Read == r.Primary && r.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote()
    51	}

   116		// checkpoint's format across both git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex
   117		// ID on the branch or a migrated ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo
   118		// handles either format without reconfiguring. Creates still go through

   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.

   181	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
   182	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
   185	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
   186	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
   187	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
   189	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
   190		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {

   192		}

   194		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
   195		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
   196			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
   197				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)

   204			// and dropped; never pay on-demand ref-fetch network probes for them.

   212		}

    41	// Four requests are session-level (Session, ReservedSession, SessionTranscript,
    42	// SessionSummary) and one is checkpoint-level (CheckpointAttribution). Adding
    43	// a write operation is a new request type plus one dispatch case in every
    44	// backend. The Store interface stays unchanged, so seam tests must exercise the
    45	// full union because Go does not exhaustively check type switches.
    46	type WriteRequest interface {
    47		isWriteRequest()
    48	}
    49	
    50	// Session creates or replaces a session document within a checkpoint,
    51	// materializing the checkpoint on its first session. (session-level)
    52	type Session WriteOptions
    53	
    54	// ReservedSession creates or replaces a session using an ID that was persisted
    55	// before the write began. Its ID kind identifies the backend that minted it, so
    56	// retries remain readable even if the configured primary changed meanwhile.
    57	type ReservedSession WriteOptions
    58	
    59	// SessionTranscript replaces a session's transcript, prompts, and skill events
    60	// at stop time without clobbering sibling fields. (session-level)
    61	type SessionTranscript UpdateOptions
    62	
    63	// SessionSummary rewrites only the summary of the checkpoint's latest session.
    64	// (session-level)
    65	type SessionSummary struct {
    66		CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
    67		Summary      *Summary
    68	}
    69	
    70	// CheckpointAttribution rewrites the checkpoint root's combined attribution
    71	// across all sessions. (checkpoint-level)
    72	//
    73	//nolint:revive // CheckpointAttribution stutter is accepted — the name makes the checkpoint (vs session) tier explicit.
    74	type CheckpointAttribution struct {
    75		CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
    76		Attribution  *Attribution
    77	}
    78	
    79	func (Session) isWriteRequest()               {}
    80	func (ReservedSession) isWriteRequest()       {}
    81	func (SessionTranscript) isWriteRequest()     {}
    82	func (SessionSummary) isWriteRequest()        {}
    83	func (CheckpointAttribution) isWriteRequest() {}
    84	
    85	// Writer is the persistent-store write surface: a single Write that accepts any
    86	// WriteRequest. It is the natural type for mirror fan-out.
    87	type Writer interface {
    88		Write(ctx context.Context, req WriteRequest) error
    89	}
    90	
    91	// ReadCheckpoint reads a checkpoint summary and normalizes a nil store response
    92	// into ErrCheckpointNotFound.
    93	func ReadCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, reader CheckpointReader, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error) {
    94		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
    95			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
    96		}
    97	
    98		summary, err := reader.Read(ctx, checkpointID)
    99		if err != nil {
   100			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read persistent checkpoint: %w", err)
   101		}
   102		if summary == nil {
   103			return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   104		}
   105		return summary, nil
   106	}
   107	
   108	// ReadLatestSessionContent reads the latest session from an already-resolved
   109	// session reader and summary.
   110	func ReadLatestSessionContent(ctx context.Context, reader SessionReader, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, summary *CheckpointSummary) (*SessionContent, error) {
   111		if summary == nil || len(summary.Sessions) == 0 {
   112			return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   113		}
   114		latestIndex := len(summary.Sessions) - 1
   115		content, err := reader.ReadSessionContent(ctx, checkpointID, latestIndex)
   116		if err != nil {
   117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read session %d content: %w", latestIndex, err)
   118		}
   119		return content, nil
   120	}
   121	
   122	// ReadRawSessionLogForCheckpoint reads a checkpoint's latest-session transcript;
   123	// it needs both reader tiers (resolve the checkpoint, then its latest session).
   124	func ReadRawSessionLogForCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, reader interface {
   125		CheckpointReader
   126		SessionReader
   127	}, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) ([]byte, string, error) {
   128		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   129			return nil, "", err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   130		}
   131	
   132		summary, err := ReadCheckpoint(ctx, reader, checkpointID)
   133		if err != nil {
   134			return nil, "", err
   135		}
   136	
   137		content, err := ReadLatestSessionContent(ctx, reader, checkpointID, summary)
   138		if err != nil {
   139			return nil, "", err
   140		}
   141		return content.Transcript, content.Metadata.SessionID, nil
   142	}

    13	// OpenOptions configures Open. The zero value uses the default committed-ref
    14	// topology and attaches no blob fetcher.
    15	type OpenOptions struct {
    16		// BlobFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand blob fetcher. The checkpoint
    17		// package cannot resolve it itself, so the CLI layer injects it here and
    18		// Open attaches it to the constructed store(s). nil leaves on-demand
    19		// fetching off.
    20		BlobFetcher BlobFetchFunc
    21	
    22		// RefFetcher is the CLI-level on-demand checkpoint-ref fetcher, used by the
    23		// git-refs backend to resolve a checkpoint ref missing locally. nil leaves
    24		// reads local-only; ignored by the git-branch backend.
    25		RefFetcher RefFetchFunc
    26	
    27		// MetadataBranchFetcher is the CLI-level v1-metadata-branch fetcher, used by
    28		// the git-branch backend to resolve a metadata branch missing both locally
    29		// and on origin (the shape a fresh clone with a dedicated checkpoint_remote
    30		// has). nil leaves reads local-only; ignored by the git-refs backend. Wire it
    31		// only on foreground read paths — see MetadataBranchFetchFunc.
    32		MetadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    33	
    34		// RemoteRefLister is the CLI-level checkpoint-ref enumerator, used by the
    35		// git-refs backend's List to discover checkpoints present on the checkpoint
    36		// remote but not yet local (see RemoteRefListFunc). It only fires on a
    37		// context marked by WithRemoteListDiscovery. nil (or an unmarked context)
    38		// leaves List local-only; ignored by the git-branch backend.
    39		RemoteRefLister RemoteRefListFunc
    40	
    41		// Refs overrides the default committed-ref topology. A non-nil value wins,
    42		// e.g. attach pins reads to Primary via PrimaryAsRead().
    43		Refs *PersistentRefs
    44	
    45		// ReadRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain (elected sync
    46		// remote first, then the legacy origin tier). The checkpoint package
    47		// cannot resolve the election itself, so cli/strategy callers inject it
    48		// here (strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes). The git-branch store's committed
    49		// reads consult these remotes' tracking refs after the local tree, selecting
    50		// by requested checkpoint rather than branch existence. This is a pure read;
    51		// local refs are never written from the chain. nil keeps the legacy
    52		// origin-only fallback.
    53		ReadRemotes []string
    54	}
    55	
    56	// PrimaryIsRefs reports whether the configured primary backend is the git-refs
    57	// per-checkpoint store. It centralizes the topology check so push/pre-push code
    58	// does not compare backend-type strings itself. A nil config (default) is the
    59	// git-branch backend, so this returns false.
    60	func PrimaryIsRefs(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) bool {
    61		return cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type == BackendTypeGitRefs
    62	}
    63	
    64	// Stores is the facade returned by Open: the persistent store plus the git-only
    65	// ephemeral (shadow-branch) capability and resolved committed-ref topology.
    66	type Stores struct {
    67		// Persistent is the committed store that serves permanent reads and writes.
    68		Persistent PersistentStore
    69	
    70		ephemeral EphemeralStore
    71		refs      PersistentRefs
    72	}
    73	
    74	// Open resolves the checkpoint storage topology and constructs the backing
    75	// store(s). It keeps ref resolution, backend selection, and blob-fetcher wiring
    76	// in one place. The primary is built through the backend registry; with no
    77	// checkpoints config it resolves to the git-branch backend with no mirrors, so
    78	// default behavior is unchanged. When mirrors are configured, the persistent
    79	// store is a fan-out wrapper (reads from primary, best-effort writes to mirrors).
    80	//
    81	// Backend selection is read via settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig, which resolves
    82	// like settings.Load: from the context's worktree root if set, else relative to
    83	// the current working directory — not from repo. Callers opening a repository
    84	// that is not the cwd should wrap ctx with that worktree root (as dispatch does).
    85	// Resolution is fail-soft about settings CONTENT: a missing settings file, a
    86	// whole-file JSON syntax error, or unrelated invalid fields all yield the
    87	// default git-branch backend with no mirrors, preserving default behavior.
    88	//
    89	// It is not fail-soft about which repository this is. A worktree root that will
    90	// not resolve is returned as an error rather than defaulted, because the backend
    91	// choice would then be made for a repo we could not identify — and the settings
    92	// file that names it is the one we failed to find. That failure is unreachable
    93	// from a command in practice: the root pre-run refuses to run at all when the
    94	// worktree root does not resolve. LoadCheckpointsConfig draws the same line.
    95	func Open(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, opts OpenOptions) (*Stores, error) {
    96		refs := resolveOpenRefs(ctx, opts)
    97		env := OpenEnv{Repo: repo, BlobFetcher: opts.BlobFetcher, RefFetcher: opts.RefFetcher, RemoteRefLister: opts.RemoteRefLister, MetadataBranchFetcher: opts.MetadataBranchFetcher, Refs: refs, ReadRemotes: opts.ReadRemotes}
    98	
    99		cfg, err := settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig(ctx)
   100		if err != nil {
   101			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoints config: %w", err)
   102		}
   103	
   104		primaryType := resolvePrimaryType(cfg)
   105		primary, err := buildPrimary(ctx, env, primaryType, primaryConfig(cfg))
   106		if err != nil {
   107			return nil, err
   108		}
   109		mirrors, err := buildMirrors(ctx, env, cfg, primaryType)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			return nil, err
   112		}
   113		writer := newFanoutStore(primary, mirrors)
   114	
   115		// Kind routing: resolve id-keyed reads and backfill writes by the
   116		// checkpoint's format across both git backends (a ULID lives in refs, a hex
   117		// ID on the branch or a migrated ref), so a coexisting / mid-migration repo
   118		// handles either format without reconfiguring. Creates still go through
   119		// writer (configured primary + mirrors).
   120		branchStore, refsStore, err := buildKindReadStores(ctx, env, primaryType, primary)
   121		if err != nil {
   122			return nil, err
   123		}
   124	
   125		return &Stores{
   126			Persistent: newKindRoutingStore(writer, branchStore, refsStore, primaryType),
   127			ephemeral:  newEphemeralStore(repo, refs),
   128			refs:       refs,
   129		}, nil
   130	}
   131	
   132	// buildKindReadStores returns the git-branch and git-refs read stores used for
   133	// id-kind read routing, reusing the already-built primary for whichever kind it
   134	// is and constructing the sibling. A non-branch/refs git-backed primary (not a
   135	// real configuration today, since buildPrimary only accepts git-backed backends)
   136	// yields both freshly built git stores.
   137	func buildKindReadStores(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, primaryType string, primary PersistentStore) (branch, refs PersistentStore, err error) {
   138		switch primaryType {
   139		case BackendTypeGitBranch:
   140			branch = primary
   141			refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   142		case BackendTypeGitRefs:
   143			refs = primary
   144			branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil)
   145		default:
   146			if branch, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitBranch, nil); err == nil {
   147				refs, err = build(ctx, env, BackendTypeGitRefs, nil)
   148			}
   149		}
   150		return branch, refs, err
   151	}
   152	
   153	// resolvePrimaryType returns the configured primary backend type, defaulting to
   154	// the git-branch backend when none is configured.
   155	func resolvePrimaryType(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) string {
   156		if cfg != nil && cfg.Primary.Type != "" {
   157			return cfg.Primary.Type
   158		}
   159		return BackendTypeGitBranch
   160	}
   161	
   162	// primaryConfig returns the primary backend's config block, if any.
   163	func primaryConfig(cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig) json.RawMessage {
   164		if cfg == nil {
   165			return nil
   166		}
   167		return cfg.Primary.Config
   168	}
   169	
   170	// buildPrimary constructs the primary persistent store. The primary must be a
   171	// git-backed backend: attach, resume, push, doctor, cleanup, and OPF all drive
   172	// the primary's record through the repo and its refs, so a non-git-backed
   173	// primary is rejected rather than silently half-supported.
   174	func buildPrimary(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, typ string, raw json.RawMessage) (PersistentStore, error) {
   175		if err := ValidatePrimaryBackend(typ); err != nil {
   176			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.primary: %w", err)
   177		}
   178		return build(ctx, env, typ, raw)
   179	}
   180	
   181	// buildMirrors constructs the mirror writers. Each backend type may appear at
   182	// most once across the topology (primary + mirrors), so a mirror cannot reuse
   183	// the primary's type or another mirror's. This is the conservative form of "no
   184	// two backends may write the same target": today two backends of the same type
   185	// share the same refs/storage, so a duplicate type is a guaranteed collision
   186	// (e.g. a git-branch mirror under a git-branch primary would double-write the v1
   187	// branch). A future per-mirror config (same backend type pointed at a distinct
   188	// repo/refs) could relax this; for now it is one of each type.
   189	func buildMirrors(ctx context.Context, env OpenEnv, cfg *settings.CheckpointsConfig, primaryType string) ([]Writer, error) {
   190		if cfg == nil || len(cfg.Mirrors) == 0 {
   191			return nil, nil
   192		}
   193		seen := map[string]bool{primaryType: true}
   194		mirrors := make([]Writer, 0, len(cfg.Mirrors))
   195		for i, m := range cfg.Mirrors {
   196			if _, err := lookupBackend(m.Type); err != nil {
   197				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   198			}
   199			if seen[m.Type] {
   200				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: backend type %q is already used by the primary or another mirror; each backend type may appear at most once", i, m.Type)
   201			}
   202			seen[m.Type] = true
   203			// Mirrors are best-effort write-only copies whose failures are logged
   204			// and dropped; never pay on-demand ref-fetch network probes for them.
   205			mirrorEnv := env
   206			mirrorEnv.RefFetcher = nil
   207			store, err := build(ctx, mirrorEnv, m.Type, m.Config)
   208			if err != nil {
   209				return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoints.mirrors[%d]: %w", i, err)
   210			}
   211			mirrors = append(mirrors, store)
   212		}
   213		return mirrors, nil
   214	}
   215	
   216	func resolveOpenRefs(ctx context.Context, opts OpenOptions) PersistentRefs {
   217		if opts.Refs != nil {
   218			return *opts.Refs
   219		}
   220		return ResolveRefs(ctx)
   221	}
   222	
   223	// Ephemeral returns the git-backed shadow-branch (temporary) store.
   224	func (s *Stores) Ephemeral() EphemeralStore { return s.ephemeral }
   225	
   226	// Refs returns the resolved committed-ref topology.
   227	func (s *Stores) Refs() PersistentRefs { return s.refs }

    17	// treeWriter holds the repo-only machinery for building a single checkpoint's
    18	// subtree from write requests: entry builders, transcript/session writers, and
    19	// the per-request appliers (applySessionWrite / applyTranscriptBackfill /
    20	// applySummaryBackfill / applyAttributionBackfill). It is independent of where
    21	// the resulting subtree is committed, so both the git-branch store (which nests
    22	// the subtree under <shard>/<id>/ on the v1 branch) and the git-refs store
    23	// (which keeps it at the root of a per-checkpoint ref) embed it and share this
    24	// code.
    25	type treeWriter struct {
    26		repo *git.Repository
    27	}
    28	
    29	// GitStore is the committed (persistent) checkpoint store. Writes target
    30	// refs.Primary; committed reads resolve against refs.Read. The temporary
    31	// shadow-branch surface lives in ephemeralStore. It embeds *treeWriter for the
    32	// shared subtree-building machinery.
    33	type GitStore struct {
    34		*treeWriter
    35	
    36		refs                  PersistentRefs
    37		blobFetcher           BlobFetchFunc
    38		metadataBranchFetcher MetadataBranchFetchFunc
    39		// metadataBranchFetchTried latches the one recovery attempt per store; see
    40		// tryFetchMetadataBranch.
    41		metadataBranchFetchTried bool
    42		// readRemotes is the ordered checkpoint read-candidate chain consulted by
    43		// committed reads after the local tree; see OpenOptions.ReadRemotes. nil
    44		// means the legacy origin-only fallback.
    45		readRemotes []string
    46	}
    47	
    48	// ephemeralStore is the git shadow-branch (temporary) checkpoint store. It is
    49	// an independent type from GitStore; the two share only package-level helpers.
    50	type ephemeralStore struct {
    51		repo *git.Repository
    52		refs PersistentRefs
    53	}
    54	
    55	// newEphemeralStore creates the shadow-branch store for the given repository
    56	// and committed-metadata topology (it consults refs.Primary to recognize the
    57	// committed branch when listing shadow branches).
    58	func newEphemeralStore(repo *git.Repository, refs PersistentRefs) *ephemeralStore {
    59		return &ephemeralStore{repo: repo, refs: refs}
    60	}
    61	
    62	// NewEphemeralStore constructs the git shadow-branch (temporary) checkpoint
    63	// store. Most callers reach it via Open(...).Ephemeral(); this direct
    64	// constructor exists for benchmarks and tests that exercise the shadow-branch
    65	// surface without the full facade.
    66	func NewEphemeralStore(repo *git.Repository, refs PersistentRefs) EphemeralStore {
    67		return newEphemeralStore(repo, refs)
    68	}
    69	
    70	// NewGitStore creates a checkpoint store backed by the given git repository
    71	// and committed-metadata topology. Pass DefaultV1Refs() for the v1-only default
    72	// or ResolveRefs(ctx) in code paths that honor settings.
    73	func NewGitStore(repo *git.Repository, refs PersistentRefs) *GitStore {
    74		return &GitStore{treeWriter: &treeWriter{repo: repo}, refs: refs}
    75	}
    76	
    77	// SetBlobFetcher configures the store to automatically fetch missing blobs
    78	// on demand when reading from metadata trees.
    79	func (s *GitStore) SetBlobFetcher(f BlobFetchFunc) {
    80		s.blobFetcher = f
    81	}
    82	
    83	// SetReadRemotes configures the ordered checkpoint read-candidate remotes
    84	// (elected sync remote first, then the legacy origin tier) whose tracking
    85	// refs committed reads consult after the local tree. Selection happens by
    86	// requested checkpoint, so an existing but incomplete tree does not mask a
    87	// later candidate. This is a pure read — the chain never seeds or advances
    88	// local refs. nil keeps the legacy origin-only fallback.
    89	func (s *GitStore) SetReadRemotes(remotes []string) {
    90		s.readRemotes = remotes
    91	}
    92	
    93	// SetMetadataBranchFetcher configures the store to fetch the metadata branch
    94	// from the checkpoint remote when it is missing both locally and on origin.
    95	// See MetadataBranchFetchFunc for when it is appropriate to wire this.
    96	func (s *GitStore) SetMetadataBranchFetcher(f MetadataBranchFetchFunc) {
    97		s.metadataBranchFetcher = f
    98	}
    99	
   100	// Repository returns the underlying git repository.
   101	func (s *GitStore) Repository() *git.Repository {
   102		return s.repo
   103	}
   104	
   105	// Refs returns the committed-metadata topology the store was constructed with.
   106	func (s *GitStore) Refs() PersistentRefs {
   107		return s.refs
   108	}
   109	
   110	// PersistentReadRef returns the ref that committed-checkpoint reads resolve against.
   111	func (s *GitStore) PersistentReadRef() plumbing.ReferenceName {
   112		return s.refs.Read
   113	}
   114	
   115	func (s *GitStore) updatePrimaryRef(ctx context.Context, build func(parentHash, rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash) (plumbing.Hash, error)) error {
   116		return updatePersistentRef(ctx, s.repo, s.refs.Primary, func() (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   117			parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := s.getSessionsBranchRef()
   118			if err != nil {
   119				return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   120			}
   121			newHash, buildErr := build(parentHash, rootTreeHash)
   122			return newHash, parentHash, buildErr
   123		})

    12	// PersistentRefs is the committed-metadata ref topology.
    13	type PersistentRefs struct {
    14		Primary plumbing.ReferenceName
    15		Read    plumbing.ReferenceName
    16		Push    []plumbing.ReferenceName
    17	
    18		// localReadOnly pins reads to the local Read ref with no remote-tracking
    19		// tiers at all — set via PrimaryAsLocalRead. Guards (attach's
    20		// local-presence gates) that must answer "would the next LOCAL write see
    21		// this checkpoint?" need it: the ordinary read chain selects per
    22		// checkpoint across local and remote-tracking trees, so a checkpoint
    23		// present only on a remote would otherwise read as present and a write
    24		// based on the stale local branch would clobber the remote on push.
    25		localReadOnly bool
    26	}
    27	
    28	// DefaultV1Refs returns the v1-only topology.
    29	func DefaultV1Refs() PersistentRefs {
    30		v1Branch := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
    31		return PersistentRefs{
    32			Primary: v1Branch,
    33			Read:    v1Branch,
    34			Push:    []plumbing.ReferenceName{v1Branch},
    35		}
    36	}
    37	
    38	// PrimaryFetchableFromRemote reports whether Primary has a remote-tracking
    39	// shadow on whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    40	// remote-tracking ref).
    41	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() bool {
    42		return r.Primary.IsBranch() && slices.Contains(r.Push, r.Primary)
    43	}
    44	
    45	// ReadBootstrappableFromRemote reports whether reads can be bootstrapped from
    46	// whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    47	// remote-tracking ref): true when reads target Primary and Primary is
    48	// fetchable from a remote, and the topology was not pinned local-only.
    49	func (r PersistentRefs) ReadBootstrappableFromRemote() bool {
    50		return !r.localReadOnly && r.Read == r.Primary && r.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote()
    51	}
    52	
    53	// PrimaryAsRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary.
    54	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsRead() PersistentRefs {
    55		r.Read = r.Primary
    56		return r
    57	}
    58	
    59	// PrimaryAsLocalRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary and
    60	// every remote read tier disabled — see the localReadOnly field for when a
    61	// caller needs this instead of PrimaryAsRead.
    62	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsLocalRead() PersistentRefs {
    63		r.Read = r.Primary
    64		r.localReadOnly = true
    65		return r
    66	}
    67	
    68	// ResolveRefs returns the committed metadata topology.
    69	func ResolveRefs(_ context.Context) PersistentRefs {
    70		return DefaultV1Refs()
    71	}

    40	// remote-tracking ref).
    41	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryFetchableFromRemote() bool {
    42		return r.Primary.IsBranch() && slices.Contains(r.Push, r.Primary)
    43	}
    44	
    45	// ReadBootstrappableFromRemote reports whether reads can be bootstrapped from
    46	// whichever remote carries checkpoint data (the caller supplies the
    47	// remote-tracking ref): true when reads target Primary and Primary is
    48	// fetchable from a remote, and the topology was not pinned local-only.
    49	func (r PersistentRefs) ReadBootstrappableFromRemote() bool {
    50		return !r.localReadOnly && r.Read == r.Primary && r.PrimaryFetchableFromRemote()
    51	}
    52	
    53	// PrimaryAsRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary.
    54	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsRead() PersistentRefs {
    55		r.Read = r.Primary
    56		return r
    57	}
    58	
    59	// PrimaryAsLocalRead returns a copy of r with Read pinned to Primary and
    60	// every remote read tier disabled — see the localReadOnly field for when a
    61	// caller needs this instead of PrimaryAsRead.
    62	func (r PersistentRefs) PrimaryAsLocalRead() PersistentRefs {
    63		r.Read = r.Primary
    64		r.localReadOnly = true
    65		return r
    66	}

    68	// ResolveRefs returns the committed metadata topology.
    69	func ResolveRefs(_ context.Context) PersistentRefs {
    70		return DefaultV1Refs()

     2	
     3	import (

     5		"fmt"

     8	)
     9	
    10	// CheckpointReader provides read access to checkpoint-level persistent data.
    11	//
    12	//nolint:revive // CheckpointReader stutter is accepted — the name marks the checkpoint (vs session) read tier.
    13	type CheckpointReader interface {
    14		Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error)
    15		List(ctx context.Context) ([]CheckpointInfo, error)
    16	}
    17	
    18	// SessionReader provides read access to session-level data within a checkpoint.
    19	type SessionReader interface {
    20		ReadSessionContent(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*SessionContent, error)
    21		ReadSessionMetadata(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*Metadata, error)
    22		ReadSessionPrompts(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (string, error)
    23		ReadSessionMetadataAndPrompts(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*Metadata, string, error)
    24	}
    25	
    26	// PersistentStore provides the production persistent checkpoint storage surface:
    27	// checkpoint-level reads, session-level reads, and the unified Write. Writes go
    28	// through Writer.Write(ctx, WriteRequest); the concrete per-operation methods
    29	// live on the git implementation as the methods Write dispatches to.
    30	type PersistentStore interface {
    31		CheckpointReader
    32		SessionReader
    33		Writer
    34	}
    35	
    36	// WriteRequest is a single persistent-store write command. The set is closed to
    37	// other packages: only types in this package can implement it, sealed via the
    38	// unexported isWriteRequest marker. A store dispatches on the concrete type; a
    39	// mirror/fan-out store forwards the same value to each backend's Write.
    40	//
    41	// Four requests are session-level (Session, ReservedSession, SessionTranscript,
    42	// SessionSummary) and one is checkpoint-level (CheckpointAttribution). Adding
    43	// a write operation is a new request type plus one dispatch case in every
    44	// backend. The Store interface stays unchanged, so seam tests must exercise the
    45	// full union because Go does not exhaustively check type switches.
    46	type WriteRequest interface {
    47		isWriteRequest()
    48	}
    49	
    50	// Session creates or replaces a session document within a checkpoint,
    51	// materializing the checkpoint on its first session. (session-level)
    52	type Session WriteOptions
    53	
    54	// ReservedSession creates or replaces a session using an ID that was persisted
    55	// before the write began. Its ID kind identifies the backend that minted it, so
    56	// retries remain readable even if the configured primary changed meanwhile.
    57	type ReservedSession WriteOptions
    58	
    59	// SessionTranscript replaces a session's transcript, prompts, and skill events
    60	// at stop time without clobbering sibling fields. (session-level)
    61	type SessionTranscript UpdateOptions
    62	
    63	// SessionSummary rewrites only the summary of the checkpoint's latest session.
    64	// (session-level)
    65	type SessionSummary struct {
    66		CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
    67		Summary      *Summary
    68	}
    69	
    70	// CheckpointAttribution rewrites the checkpoint root's combined attribution
    71	// across all sessions. (checkpoint-level)
    72	//
    73	//nolint:revive // CheckpointAttribution stutter is accepted — the name makes the checkpoint (vs session) tier explicit.
    74	type CheckpointAttribution struct {
    75		CheckpointID id.CheckpointID
    76		Attribution  *Attribution
    77	}
    78	
    79	func (Session) isWriteRequest()               {}
    80	func (ReservedSession) isWriteRequest()       {}
    81	func (SessionTranscript) isWriteRequest()     {}
    82	func (SessionSummary) isWriteRequest()        {}
    83	func (CheckpointAttribution) isWriteRequest() {}
    84	
    85	// Writer is the persistent-store write surface: a single Write that accepts any
    86	// WriteRequest. It is the natural type for mirror fan-out.
    87	type Writer interface {
    88		Write(ctx context.Context, req WriteRequest) error
    89	}
    90	
    91	// ReadCheckpoint reads a checkpoint summary and normalizes a nil store response
    92	// into ErrCheckpointNotFound.
    93	func ReadCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, reader CheckpointReader, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error) {
    94		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
    95			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
    96		}
    97	
    98		summary, err := reader.Read(ctx, checkpointID)
    99		if err != nil {
   100			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read persistent checkpoint: %w", err)
   101		}
   102		if summary == nil {
   103			return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   104		}
   105		return summary, nil
   106	}
   107	
   108	// ReadLatestSessionContent reads the latest session from an already-resolved
   109	// session reader and summary.
   110	func ReadLatestSessionContent(ctx context.Context, reader SessionReader, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, summary *CheckpointSummary) (*SessionContent, error) {
   111		if summary == nil || len(summary.Sessions) == 0 {
   112			return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   113		}
   114		latestIndex := len(summary.Sessions) - 1
   115		content, err := reader.ReadSessionContent(ctx, checkpointID, latestIndex)
   116		if err != nil {
   117			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read session %d content: %w", latestIndex, err)
   118		}
   119		return content, nil
   120	}
   121	
   122	// ReadRawSessionLogForCheckpoint reads a checkpoint's latest-session transcript;
   123	// it needs both reader tiers (resolve the checkpoint, then its latest session).
   124	func ReadRawSessionLogForCheckpoint(ctx context.Context, reader interface {
   125		CheckpointReader
   126		SessionReader
   127	}, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) ([]byte, string, error) {
   128		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   129			return nil, "", err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   130		}
   131	
   132		summary, err := ReadCheckpoint(ctx, reader, checkpointID)
   133		if err != nil {
   134			return nil, "", err
   135		}
   136	
   137		content, err := ReadLatestSessionContent(ctx, reader, checkpointID, summary)
   138		if err != nil {
   139			return nil, "", err
   140		}
   141		return content.Transcript, content.Metadata.SessionID, nil
   142	}

   508	// CondenseSession condenses a session's shadow branch to permanent storage.

   510	// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpoint_id[:2]>/<checkpoint_id[2:]>/
   511	// Uses checkpoint.PersistentStore.Write with a checkpoint.Session request for persistent storage.
   512	//
   513	// For mid-session commits (no Stop/SaveStep called yet), the shadow branch may not exist.
   514	// In this case, data is extracted from the live transcript instead.
   515	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, state *SessionState, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, opts ...condenseOpts) (*CondenseResult, error) {
   516		ag, _ := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType) //nolint:errcheck // ag may be nil for unknown agent types; callers use type assertions so nil is safe
   517		var o condenseOpts
   518		if len(opts) > 0 {
   519			o = opts[0]
   520		}
   521		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   522		condenseStart := time.Now()
   523		policy, err := readLocalCheckpointPolicy(logCtx, repo)
   524		if err != nil {
   525			return nil, fmt.Errorf("checkpoint policy could not be read: %w", err)
   526		}
   527		if !checkpointpolicy.CanSatisfyPolicy(policy) {
   528			warnIfCheckpointPolicyNeedsUpgrade(logCtx, policy)
   529			return nil, errors.New("checkpoint policy cannot be satisfied by this Entire CLI")
   530		}

   532		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   533		ref, hasShadowBranch := resolveShadowRef(repo, shadowBranchName, o.shadowRef)

   535		// Re-resolve transcript path before any reads — handles agents that relocate
   536		// transcripts mid-session (e.g., Cursor CLI flat → nested layout change).
   537		// Errors are ignored; downstream readers handle missing transcripts gracefully.
   538		resolveTranscriptPath(state) //nolint:errcheck,gosec // best-effort; downstream readers handle missing files

   541		_, extractSessionDataSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_session_data")
   542		var shadowHash plumbing.Hash
   543		if hasShadowBranch {
   544			shadowHash = ref.Hash()
   545		}
   546		sessionData, extractErr := s.extractOrCreateSessionData(ctx, repo, ag, shadowHash, hasShadowBranch, state)
   547		if extractErr != nil {
   548			extractSessionDataSpan.RecordError(extractErr)
   549			extractSessionDataSpan.End()
   550			return nil, extractErr
   551		}
   552		extractSessionDataSpan.End()
   553		extractDuration := time.Since(extractStart)
   554	
   555		// Backfill session state token usage from the freshly-extracted transcript.
   556		// Copilot CLI writes session.shutdown after the hooks return, so by condensation
   557		// time we can recover the authoritative full-session total from the transcript
   558		// while keeping checkpoint metadata scoped to CheckpointTranscriptStart. The
   559		// recompute drops SubagentTokens (subagentsDir=""); the helper preserves the
   560		// cumulative subagent total across the backfill so resetCheckpointWindow's
   561		// baseline does not regress to nil (finding 019f5ebf-a57e).
   562		applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage(ctx, ag, state, sessionData.Transcript, sessionData.TokenUsage)
   563	
   564		if !hasTokenUsageData(sessionData.TokenUsage) && hasTokenUsageData(state.CheckpointTokenUsage) {
   565			// Whole-value fallback: accumulateTokenUsage already carries SubagentTokens.
   566			sessionData.TokenUsage = accumulateTokenUsage(nil, state.CheckpointTokenUsage)
   567		} else {
   568			// Refill only the subagent total the recompute dropped. Runs after
   569			// applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage, which needs the usage without it.
   570			sessionData.TokenUsage = withSubagentTokensFrom(sessionData.TokenUsage, state.CheckpointTokenUsage)
   571		}
   572	
   573		// Backfill the model from the transcript for agents that don't report it via
   574		// hooks (e.g., Pi records message.model but its hook events carry no model
   575		// field). Only fills when the model is otherwise unknown — hook-reported
   576		// models take precedence.
   577		if state.ModelName == "" {
   578			if model := sessionStateBackfillModel(ctx, ag, sessionData.Transcript); model != "" {
   579				state.ModelName = model
   580			}
   581		}

   585		}
   586	
   587		filterFilesTouched(sessionData, committedFiles, state)
   588	
   589		// sessionData.Transcript is left as the raw transcript; only the sanitized,
   590		// externalized, redacted copy is stored.
   591		externalizedTranscript, extractedAssets, transcriptSizeBaseline := prepareTranscriptForStorage(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, sessionData.Transcript)
   592	
   593		redactedTranscript, redactDuration := redactOrDrop(logCtx, repo, state.SessionID, externalizedTranscript, checkpointID)
   594		if skipped := skipIfPostRedactionEmpty(logCtx, redactedTranscript, sessionData, state, checkpointID); skipped != nil {
   595			return skipped, nil
   596		}
   597	
   598		// Telemetry-only search probe, computed exactly once for every result this
   599		// function can return (the recovery result below included) so no
   600		// construction site can ship the zero value by omission — the fabricated
   601		// negative searchProbe.measured exists to catch. Gated: the scan is a
   602		// full-transcript pass, and only the PostCommit path, with telemetry
   603		// enabled, has a reader for it. detectSearchUsage maps a nil agent or
   604		// empty transcript to unsupported, which is the honest answer for the
   605		// no-transcript extraction branch.
   606		if o.searchProbeAllowed != nil && o.searchProbeAllowed() {
   607			sessionData.SearchProbe = detectSearchUsage(ag, sessionData.Transcript)
   608		}
   609	
   610		// Capture agent sidecar images (e.g. Cursor's SQLite store) after the skip
   611		// check, so the sqlite3 shell-out is avoided when the checkpoint is discarded.
   612		extractedAssets = append(extractedAssets, sidecarSessionImages(ctx, logCtx, ag, state)...)
   613	
   614		// Materialize this session's subagent task records (#2058): every
   615		// completed-or-in-flight record's transcript is resolved, redacted, and
   616		// stored under this checkpoint's tasks/<tool-use-id>/ subtree.
   617		taskPayloads, extractedAssets := s.materializeTaskRecords(ctx, logCtx, ag, state, extractedAssets)
   618	
   619		store, err := s.getPersistentStore(ctx, repo)
   620		if err != nil {
   621			return nil, err
   622		}
   623		recovery := recoverInterruptedCondensation(
   624			ctx, logCtx,
   625			o.reconcileInterrupted && state.NeedsCondensationRecovery(),
   626			store, state, redactedTranscript, extractedAssets, sessionData, transcriptSizeBaseline,
   627		)
   628		if recovery.done {
   629			return recovery.result, recovery.err
   630		}
   631	
   632		writeOpts, attributionDuration, newSkillEvents := buildCondensationWriteOptions(
   633			ctx, repo, ref, state, sessionData, redactedTranscript, extractedAssets,
   634			taskPayloads, checkpointID, shadowBranchName, o,
   635		)
   636	
   637		writeV1Start := time.Now()
   638		writeCtx, writeCommittedSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_committed_v1")
   639		writeRequest := condensationSessionWriteRequest(writeOpts)
   640		if err := store.Write(writeCtx, writeRequest); err != nil {
   641			writeCommittedSpan.RecordError(err)
   642			writeCommittedSpan.End()
   643			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
   644		}
   645		writeCommittedSpan.End()
   646		writeV1Duration := time.Since(writeV1Start)
   647	
   648		// Deferred prompt-window reset: a checkpoint was written, so the window base
   649		// must be re-anchored — but not now. We defer until the next counted turn (in
   650		// persistEventMetadataToState) so two checkpoints with no prompt between them
   651		// report the same count instead of the second showing 0.
   652		state.PromptWindowResetPending = true
   653	
   654		logging.Debug(logCtx, "condense timings",
   655			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   656			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   657			slog.Int64("extract_session_data_ms", extractDuration.Milliseconds()),
   658			slog.Int64("calculate_session_attribution_ms", attributionDuration.Milliseconds()),
   659			slog.Int64("redact_transcript_ms", redactDuration.Milliseconds()),
   660			slog.Int64("write_committed_v1_ms", writeV1Duration.Milliseconds()),
   661			slog.Int64("total_ms", time.Since(condenseStart).Milliseconds()),
   662			slog.Int("transcript_bytes", len(sessionData.Transcript)),
   663			slog.Int("transcript_lines", sessionData.FullTranscriptLines),
   664		)
   665	
   666		return &CondenseResult{
   667			CheckpointID:           checkpointID,
   668			SessionID:              state.SessionID,
   669			CheckpointsCount:       checkpointStepCount(state),
   670			FilesTouched:           sessionData.FilesTouched,
   671			Prompts:                sessionData.Prompts,
   672			TotalTranscriptLines:   sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
   673			TranscriptSizeBaseline: transcriptSizeBaseline,
   674			NewSkillEvents:         newSkillEvents,
   675			SearchProbe:            sessionData.SearchProbe,
   676		}, nil
   677	}

   679	// condensationSessionWriteRequest returns the write request for one
   680	// condensation. Every condensation write is ReservedSession, unconditionally.
   681	//
   682	// The tempting refinement — send ReservedSession only when this session's own
   683	// pending attempt matches the checkpoint ID, and plain Session otherwise —
   684	// is wrong, and wrong in a worse direction than the problem it solves. A
   685	// checkpoint can hold several sessions, and only the one that reserved the ID
   686	// carries the reservation in its state. Routing per session would send the
   687	// reserving session's write to the backend the ID belongs to and every sibling's
   688	// write to the configured primary, splitting one checkpoint across both
   689	// backends. Reads are not symmetrical about that: a ULID resolves from git-refs
   690	// only, so the siblings written to the branch would simply be invisible. See
   691	// TestCondensationSessionWrites_KeepSharedReservedCheckpointInOneBackend.
   692	//
   693	// The cost of routing everything by ID format is narrow. It only diverges from
   694	// the configured primary when the ID's format disagrees with the primary, and
   695	// the two fail-soft defaults agree: GenerateCheckpointID mints hex when the
   696	// checkpoints config cannot be read, and resolvePrimaryType defaults to
   697	// git-branch on the same unreadable config. Reaching a mismatch on a *fresh* ID
   698	// therefore takes a config read that succeeds for one call and fails for the
   699	// other — and even then the checkpoint stays readable, because a hex ID under a
   700	// git-refs primary falls through to the branch on read.
   701	//
   702	// If the per-checkpoint routing decision ever does need to be conditional, it
   703	// has to be made once for the whole checkpoint (from the commit trailer or a
   704	// checkpoint-level flag), never per session.
   705	func condensationSessionWriteRequest(opts cpkg.WriteOptions) cpkg.WriteRequest {
   706		return cpkg.ReservedSession(opts)
   707	}

   679	// condensationSessionWriteRequest returns the write request for one

   682	// The tempting refinement — send ReservedSession only when this session's own

   761	// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck returns true if the session should be condensed
   762	// into this commit. Two shapes skip the overlap check: an ACTIVE session with
   763	// recent interaction, and an IDLE session with a fresh task record. Both are
   764	// still subject to the read-only gate — a session with no tracked files while
   765	// another session claims the committed files is somebody else's commit. Every
   766	// other session (a stale ACTIVE one, an IDLE one with no fresh record, an ENDED
   767	// one) must show file-overlap evidence between its tracked files and the
   768	// committed files.
   769	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool, lastInteraction *time.Time, hasTaskContent bool) bool {
   770		if !h.hasNew {
   771			return false
   772		}
   773		// PrepareCommitMsg already vetted the trailer for these two shapes, and an
   774		// in-flight record has no files yet, so overlap is unsatisfiable for it.
   775		// LastInteractionTime keeps a stale ACTIVE session (agent killed without a
   776		// Stop hook) from condensing into every subsequent commit.
   777		if (isActive && isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction)) || hasTaskContent {
   778			if h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles > 0 && len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   779				logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint"), "post-commit: skipping read-only session (no tracked files, other sessions claim committed files)",
   780					slog.Bool("is_active", isActive),
   781					slog.Int("sessions_with_committed_files", h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles),
   782				)
   783				return false
   784			}
   785			return true
   786		}
   787		if len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   788			return false // No files tracked = no overlap evidence
   789		}
   790		// Only check files that were actually changed in this commit.
   791		// Without this, files that exist in the tree but weren't changed
   792		// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   793		// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   794		// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   795		var committedTouchedFiles []string
   796		for _, f := range h.filesTouchedBefore {
   797			if _, ok := h.committedFileSet[f]; ok {
   798				committedTouchedFiles = append(committedTouchedFiles, f)
   799			}
   800		}
   801		if len(committedTouchedFiles) == 0 {
   802			return false
   803		}
   804		return filesOverlapWithContent(h.ctx, h.repo, h.shadowBranchName, h.commit, committedTouchedFiles, overlapOpts{
   805			headTree:      h.headTree,
   806			shadowTree:    h.shadowTree,
   807			parentTree:    h.parentTree,
   808			hasParentTree: true,
   809		})

   862	// idleWithTaskContent reports whether state is an IDLE session with a
   863	// recently-started task record — in flight OR completed-unmaterialized (the
   864	// HasTaskContent shapes) — the second shape trusted to link and condense
   865	// commits without overlap evidence. ENDED is excluded because an ENDED

   868	// materializes them, so a stale (>24h) record must not make every later no-TTY

   874	// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck's overlap-check bypass so the trigger and
   875	// the condensation trust can never drift apart into two different rules.
   876	func idleWithTaskContent(state *SessionState, now time.Time) bool {

   542	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) handleAmendCommitMsg(ctx context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error {
   543		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")

   550		message := string(content)

   555				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),

   561		// No trailer in message — check if any session has LastCheckpointID to restore
   562		worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)

   573		// We need to match sessions whose BaseCommit equals HEAD (the commit being amended
   574		// was created from this base). This prevents stale sessions from injecting
   575		// unrelated checkpoint IDs.
   576		repo, repoErr := OpenRepository(ctx)

   578			return nil

   588		// LastCheckpointID is set after condensation completes.
   589		for _, state := range sessions {

   592			}

   621	// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   622	// Uses the session state machine to determine what action to take per session:

   625	//   - ENDED → condense if files touched, discard if empty

   628	// carried forward to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.

   630	// Shadow branches are only deleted when ALL sessions sharing the branch are non-active
   631	// and were condensed during this PostCommit.

   761	// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck returns true if the session should be condensed
   762	// into this commit. Two shapes skip the overlap check: an ACTIVE session with
   763	// recent interaction, and an IDLE session with a fresh task record. Both are
   764	// still subject to the read-only gate — a session with no tracked files while
   765	// another session claims the committed files is somebody else's commit. Every
   766	// other session (a stale ACTIVE one, an IDLE one with no fresh record, an ENDED
   767	// one) must show file-overlap evidence between its tracked files and the
   768	// committed files.
   769	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool, lastInteraction *time.Time, hasTaskContent bool) bool {
   770		if !h.hasNew {
   771			return false
   772		}
   773		// PrepareCommitMsg already vetted the trailer for these two shapes, and an
   774		// in-flight record has no files yet, so overlap is unsatisfiable for it.
   775		// LastInteractionTime keeps a stale ACTIVE session (agent killed without a
   776		// Stop hook) from condensing into every subsequent commit.
   777		if (isActive && isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction)) || hasTaskContent {
   778			if h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles > 0 && len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   779				logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint"), "post-commit: skipping read-only session (no tracked files, other sessions claim committed files)",
   780					slog.Bool("is_active", isActive),
   781					slog.Int("sessions_with_committed_files", h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles),
   782				)
   783				return false
   784			}
   785			return true
   786		}
   787		if len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   788			return false // No files tracked = no overlap evidence
   789		}
   790		// Only check files that were actually changed in this commit.
   791		// Without this, files that exist in the tree but weren't changed
   792		// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   793		// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   794		// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   795		var committedTouchedFiles []string
   796		for _, f := range h.filesTouchedBefore {
   797			if _, ok := h.committedFileSet[f]; ok {
   798				committedTouchedFiles = append(committedTouchedFiles, f)
   799			}
   800		}
   801		if len(committedTouchedFiles) == 0 {
   802			return false
   803		}
   804		return filesOverlapWithContent(h.ctx, h.repo, h.shadowBranchName, h.commit, committedTouchedFiles, overlapOpts{
   805			headTree:      h.headTree,
   806			shadowTree:    h.shadowTree,
   807			parentTree:    h.parentTree,
   808			hasParentTree: true,
   809		})
   810	}

   851	// activeSessionInteractionThreshold is the maximum age of LastInteractionTime
   852	// for an ACTIVE session to be considered genuinely active. 24h is generous
   853	// because LastInteractionTime only updates at TurnStart, not per-tool-call.
   854	const activeSessionInteractionThreshold = 24 * time.Hour

   856	// isRecentInteraction returns true if lastInteraction is non-nil and within
   857	// activeSessionInteractionThreshold of now.
   858	func isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction *time.Time) bool {
   859		return lastInteraction != nil && time.Since(*lastInteraction) < activeSessionInteractionThreshold
   860	}

   862	// idleWithTaskContent reports whether state is an IDLE session with a
   863	// recently-started task record — in flight OR completed-unmaterialized (the
   864	// HasTaskContent shapes) — the second shape trusted to link and condense
   865	// commits without overlap evidence. ENDED is excluded because an ENDED
   866	// session's records belong to its own final condensation, not to this commit.
   867	// Bounded per record's StartedAt: records persist until condensation
   868	// materializes them, so a stale (>24h) record must not make every later no-TTY
   869	// commit a trailer candidate forever. 24h matches
   870	// activeSessionInteractionThreshold's generosity.
   871	//
   872	// Shared by tryAgentCommitFastPath's eligibility check,
   873	// filterSessionsWithNewContent's trailer gate, and
   874	// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck's overlap-check bypass so the trigger and
   875	// the condensation trust can never drift apart into two different rules.
   876	func idleWithTaskContent(state *SessionState, now time.Time) bool {
   877		if state.Phase != session.PhaseIdle {
   878			return false
   879		}
   880		for _, task := range state.TaskRecords {
   881			// StartedAt, not CompletedAt: the bound must cap how long an in-flight
   882			// record confers trust, and an in-flight record has no CompletedAt.
   883			if now.Sub(task.StartedAt) < activeSessionInteractionThreshold {
   884				return true
   885			}
   886		}
   887		return false
   888	}

    79			return defaultResult
    80		}
    81		defer tty.Close()
    82	
    83		// Write to tty directly, not stderr, since git hooks may redirect stderr to /dev/null
    84		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", header)
    85		for _, line := range details {
    86			fmt.Fprintf(tty, "  %s\n", line)
    87		}
    88	
    89		// Show prompt with option descriptions
    90		fmt.Fprintf(tty, "\n%s\n", prompt)
    91		if defaultYes {
    92			fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
    93		} else {
    94			fmt.Fprint(tty, "  [y]es / [N]o / [a]lways (remember my choice): ")
    95		}
    96	
    97		// Read response
    98		reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
    99		response, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
   100		if err != nil {
   101			return defaultResult
   102		}
   103	
   104		response = strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(response))
   105		switch response {
   106		case "y", "yes":
   107			return ttyResultLink
   108		case "n", "no":
   109			return ttyResultSkip
   110		case "a", "always":
   111			return ttyResultLinkAlways
   112		default:
   113			// Empty or invalid input - use default
   114			return defaultResult
   115		}
   116	}

   118	// saveCommitLinkingAlways persists commit_linking = "always" to settings.local.json.
   119	// Uses raw JSON merge to set only the commit_linking field without affecting other
   120	// fields. This avoids writing unintended defaults (e.g., enabled: true) when the
   121	// local settings file doesn't exist yet.
   122	func saveCommitLinkingAlways(ctx context.Context) error {
   123		// Read-modify-write through the settings package: it owns the confined read
   124		// and the atomic write, and the raw map preserves every field this hook has
   125		// no opinion about.
   126		localPath, raw, _, err := settings.LoadLocalRaw(ctx)
   127		if err != nil {
   128			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // LoadLocalRaw already names the file and the failure
   129		}
   130	
   131		raw["commit_linking"] = json.RawMessage(`"` + settings.CommitLinkingAlways + `"`)
   132	
   133		if err := settings.SaveLocalRaw(localPath, raw); err != nil {
   134			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // SaveLocalRaw already names the file and the failure
   135		}
   136		return nil
   137	}

   139	// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
   140	// If the message contains only our trailer (no actual user content), strip it
   141	// so git will abort the commit due to empty message.
   142	
   143	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CommitMsg(_ context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error { //nolint:unparam // error return is part of the hook contract; callers check it
   144		content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from git hook
   145		if err != nil {
   146			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   147		}
   148	
   149		message := string(content)
   150	
   151		// Check if our trailer is present (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   152		if _, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); !found {
   153			// No trailer, nothing to do
   154			return nil
   155		}
   156	
   157		// Check if there's any user content (non-comment, non-trailer lines)
   158		if !hasUserContent(message) {
   159			// No user content - strip the trailer so git aborts
   160			message = stripCheckpointTrailer(message)
   161			if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   162				return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   163			}
   164		}
   165	
   166		return nil
   167	}
