   169	// PostRewrite is called by the git post-rewrite hook after amend/rebase
   170	// operations. It keeps session linkage aligned with rewritten commit SHAs in
   171	// the current worktree.
   172	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostRewrite(ctx context.Context, rewriteType string, r io.Reader) error {
   173		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   174		if rewriteType != "amend" && rewriteType != "rebase" {
   175			logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-rewrite: unsupported rewrite type, skipping",
   176				slog.String("rewrite_type", rewriteType),
   177			)
   178			return nil
   179		}
   180	
   181		rewrites, err := parsePostRewritePairs(r)
   182		if err != nil {
   183			return err
   184		}
   185		if len(rewrites) == 0 {
   186			return nil
   187		}
   188	
   189		worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   190		if err != nil {
   191			return nil
   192		}
   193	
   194		sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(ctx, worktreePath)
   195		if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   196			return nil
   197		}
   198	
   199		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   200		if err != nil {
   201			return nil
   202		}
   203		defer repo.Close()
   204	
   205		for _, sess := range sessions {
   206			sessionID := sess.SessionID
   207			mutErr := MutateSessionState(ctx, sessionID, func(state *SessionState) error {
   208				changed, err := s.remapSessionForRewrite(ctx, repo, state, rewrites)
   209				if err != nil {
   210					return err
   211				}
   212				if !changed {
   213					return ErrMutationSkip
   214				}
   215				logging.Info(logCtx, "post-rewrite: remapped session linkage",
   216					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   217					slog.String("rewrite_type", rewriteType),
   218					slog.String("base_commit", truncateHash(state.BaseCommit)),
   219				)
   220				return nil
   221			})
   222			if mutErr != nil && !errors.Is(mutErr, ErrStateNotFound) {
   223				logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-rewrite: failed to remap session linkage",
   224					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
   225					slog.String("error", mutErr.Error()),
   226				)
   227			}
   228		}
   229	
   230		return nil
   231	}
   232	
   233	func parsePostRewritePairs(r io.Reader) ([]rewritePair, error) {
   234		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
   235		var pairs []rewritePair
   236		for scanner.Scan() {
   237			line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
   238			if line == "" {
   239				continue
   240			}
   241			fields := strings.Fields(line)
   242			if len(fields) < 2 {
   243				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid post-rewrite mapping line: %q", line)
   244			}
   245			pairs = append(pairs, rewritePair{
   246				OldSHA: fields[0],
   247				NewSHA: fields[1],
   248			})
   249		}
   250		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
   500				if result == ttyResultSkip {
   501					logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   502						slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   503						slog.String("source", source),
   504					)
   505					return nil
   506				}
   507				if result == ttyResultLinkAlways {
   508					// Persist preference so future commits auto-link (non-fatal if it fails)
   509					if saveErr := saveCommitLinkingAlways(ctx); saveErr != nil {
   510						logging.Warn(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: failed to save commit_linking=always",
   511							slog.String("error", saveErr.Error()),
   512						)
   513					}
   514				}
   515				message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   516			}
   517		default:
   518			// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   519			message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   520		}
   521	
   522		logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   523			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   524			slog.String("source", source),
   525			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   526		)
   527	
   528		// Write updated message back
   529		_, writeCommitMessageSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_commit_message")
   530		if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // path from git hook arg
   531			writeCommitMessageSpan.RecordError(err)
   532			writeCommitMessageSpan.End()
   533			return nil
   534		}
   535		writeCommitMessageSpan.End()
   536	
   537		return nil
   538	}

   540	// handleAmendCommitMsg handles the prepare-commit-msg hook for amend operations
   541	// (source="commit"). It preserves existing trailers or restores from LastCheckpointID.
   542	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) handleAmendCommitMsg(ctx context.Context, commitMsgFile string) error {
   543		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
   544		// Read current commit message
   545		content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile) //nolint:gosec // commitMsgFile is provided by git hook
   546		if err != nil {
   547			return nil
   548		}
   549	
   550		message := string(content)
   551	
   552		// If message already has a trailer, keep it unchanged
   553		if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   554			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend preserves existing trailer",
   555				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   556				slog.String("checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   557			)
   558			return nil
   559		}
   560	
   561		// No trailer in message — check if any session has LastCheckpointID to restore
   562		worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
   563		if err != nil {
   564			return nil
   565		}
   566	
   567		sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(ctx, worktreePath)
   568		if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   569			return nil
   570		}
   571	
   572		// For amend, HEAD^ is the commit being amended, and HEAD is where we are now.
   573		// We need to match sessions whose BaseCommit equals HEAD (the commit being amended
   574		// was created from this base). This prevents stale sessions from injecting
   575		// unrelated checkpoint IDs.
   576		repo, repoErr := OpenRepository(ctx)
   577		if repoErr != nil {
   578			return nil
   579		}
   580		defer repo.Close()
   581		head, headErr := repo.Head()
   582		if headErr != nil {
   583			return nil
   584		}
   585		currentHead := head.Hash().String()
   586	
   587		// Find first matching session with LastCheckpointID to restore.
   588		// LastCheckpointID is set after condensation completes.
   589		for _, state := range sessions {
   590			if state.BaseCommit != currentHead {
   591				continue
   592			}
   593			if state.LastCheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   594				continue
   595			}
   596			cpID := state.LastCheckpointID
   597			source := "LastCheckpointID"
   598	
   599			// Restore the trailer
   600			message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, cpID)
   601			if writeErr := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); writeErr != nil { //nolint:gosec // path from git hook arg
   602				return nil
   603			}
   604	
   605			logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: restored trailer on amend",
   606				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   607				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpID.String()),
   608				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   609				slog.String("source", source),
   610			)
   611			return nil
   612		}
   613	
   614		// No checkpoint ID found - leave message unchanged
   615		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: amend with no checkpoint to restore",
   616			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   617		)
   618		return nil
   619	}

   621	// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   622	// Uses the session state machine to determine what action to take per session:
   623	//   - ACTIVE → condense immediately (each commit gets its own checkpoint)
   624	//   - IDLE → condense immediately
   625	//   - ENDED → condense if files touched, discard if empty
   626	//
   627	// After condensation for ACTIVE sessions, remaining uncommitted files are
   628	// carried forward to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.
   629	//
   630	// Shadow branches are only deleted when ALL sessions sharing the branch are non-active
   631	// and were condensed during this PostCommit.
   632	
   633	// postCommitActionHandler implements session.ActionHandler for PostCommit.
   634	// Each session in the loop gets its own handler with per-session context.
   635	// Handler methods use the *State parameter from ApplyTransition (same pointer
   636	// as the state being transitioned) rather than capturing state separately.
   637	type postCommitActionHandler struct {
   638		s                          *ManualCommitStrategy
   639		ctx                        context.Context
   640		repo                       *git.Repository
   641		checkpointID               id.CheckpointID
   642		head                       *plumbing.Reference
   643		commit                     *object.Commit
   644		newHead                    string
   645		repoDir                    string
   646		shadowBranchName           string
   647		shadowBranchesToDelete     map[string]struct{}
   648		committedFileSet           map[string]struct{}
   649		hasNew                     bool
   650		filesTouchedBefore         []string
   651		sessionsWithCommittedFiles int // number of processable sessions that have tracked files
   652	
   653		// Cached git objects — resolved once per PostCommit invocation to avoid
   654		// redundant reads across filesOverlapWithContent, filesWithRemainingAgentChanges,
   655		// CondenseSession, and calculateSessionAttributions.
   656		headTree      *object.Tree        // HEAD commit tree (shared across all sessions)
   657		parentTree    *object.Tree        // HEAD's first parent tree (shared, nil for initial commits)
   658		shadowRef     *plumbing.Reference // Per-session shadow branch ref (nil if branch doesn't exist)
   659		shadowTree    *object.Tree        // Per-session shadow commit tree (nil if branch doesn't exist)
   660		allAgentFiles map[string]struct{} // Union of all sessions' FilesTouched for cross-session attribution
   661	
   662		// Output: set by handler methods, read by caller after TransitionAndLog.
   663		// condensed is true only when CondenseSession wrote data to the metadata branch.
   664		// Both failures and skips (no transcript/files) leave condensed=false, which
   665		// correctly preserves shadow branches and defers FullyCondensed marking.
   666		condensed bool
   667		// newSkillEvents are the skill events condensation appended to session
   668		// state; the PostCommit loop forwards them to telemetry after the
   669		// session's MutateSessionState saves.
   670		newSkillEvents []agent.SkillEvent
   671		// condensedSignal is the missed-opportunity adoption signal snapshotted
   672		// by condensation; emitted by the PostCommit loop after the session's
   673		// MutateSessionState saves.
   674		condensedSignal *commitCondensedSignal
   675		// condensedTelemetry is the commit-scoped emitter; the handler passes its
   676		// memoized gate into condensation so the search-usage transcript scan is
   677		// skipped entirely when telemetry is opted out or not opted in.
   678		condensedTelemetry *commitCondensedEmitter
   679	}
   680	
   681	// searchProbeGate adapts the emitter's memoized telemetry gate to the
   682	// condenseOpts shape; nil when no emitter was wired (defensive — PostCommit
   683	// always wires one), which condensation reads as "don't scan".
   684	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) searchProbeGate() func() bool {
   685		if h.condensedTelemetry == nil {
   686			return nil
   687		}
   688		return func() bool { return h.condensedTelemetry.searchProbeAllowed(h.ctx) }
   689	}
   690	
   691	// parentCommitHash returns the first parent's hash as a string, or empty for initial commits.
   692	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) parentCommitHash() string {
   693		if h.commit.NumParents() > 0 && len(h.commit.ParentHashes) > 0 {
   694			return h.commit.ParentHashes[0].String()
   695		}
   696		return ""
   697	}

   699	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) HandleCondense(state *session.State) error {
   700		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint")
   701		hasTaskContent := idleWithTaskContent(state, time.Now())
   702		shouldCondense := h.shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(state.Phase.IsActive(), state.LastInteractionTime, hasTaskContent)
   703	
   704		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: HandleCondense decision",
   705			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   706			slog.String("phase", string(state.Phase)),
   707			slog.Bool("has_new", h.hasNew),
   708			slog.Bool("idle_with_task_content", hasTaskContent),
   709			slog.Int("task_records", len(state.TaskRecords)),
   710			slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   711			slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),
   712		)
   713	
   714		if shouldCondense {
   715			h.condensed, h.newSkillEvents, h.condensedSignal = h.s.condenseAndUpdateState(h.ctx, h.repo, h.checkpointID, state, h.head, h.shadowBranchName, h.shadowBranchesToDelete, h.committedFileSet, condenseOpts{
   716				shadowRef:          h.shadowRef,
   717				headTree:           h.headTree,
   718				parentTree:         h.parentTree,
   719				repoDir:            h.repoDir,
   720				parentCommitHash:   h.parentCommitHash(),
   721				headCommitHash:     h.newHead,
   722				allAgentFiles:      h.allAgentFiles,
   723				searchProbeAllowed: h.searchProbeGate(),
   724			})
   725		} else {
   726			h.s.updateBaseCommitIfChanged(h.ctx, state, h.newHead, h.repoDir)
   727		}
   728		return nil
   729	}

   739			slog.Int("files_touched", len(state.FilesTouched)),
   740			slog.Bool("should_condense", shouldCondense),
   741			slog.String("shadow_branch", h.shadowBranchName),

   746				shadowRef:          h.shadowRef,

   748				parentTree:         h.parentTree,
   749				repoDir:            h.repoDir,
   750				parentCommitHash:   h.parentCommitHash(),

   761	// shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck returns true if the session should be condensed
   762	// into this commit. Two shapes skip the overlap check: an ACTIVE session with
   763	// recent interaction, and an IDLE session with a fresh task record. Both are
   764	// still subject to the read-only gate — a session with no tracked files while
   765	// another session claims the committed files is somebody else's commit. Every
   766	// other session (a stale ACTIVE one, an IDLE one with no fresh record, an ENDED
   767	// one) must show file-overlap evidence between its tracked files and the
   768	// committed files.
   769	func (h *postCommitActionHandler) shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck(isActive bool, lastInteraction *time.Time, hasTaskContent bool) bool {
   770		if !h.hasNew {
   771			return false
   772		}
   773		// PrepareCommitMsg already vetted the trailer for these two shapes, and an
   774		// in-flight record has no files yet, so overlap is unsatisfiable for it.
   775		// LastInteractionTime keeps a stale ACTIVE session (agent killed without a
   776		// Stop hook) from condensing into every subsequent commit.
   777		if (isActive && isRecentInteraction(lastInteraction)) || hasTaskContent {
   778			if h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles > 0 && len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   779				logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(h.ctx, "checkpoint"), "post-commit: skipping read-only session (no tracked files, other sessions claim committed files)",
   780					slog.Bool("is_active", isActive),
   781					slog.Int("sessions_with_committed_files", h.sessionsWithCommittedFiles),
   782				)
   783				return false
   784			}
   785			return true
   786		}
   787		if len(h.filesTouchedBefore) == 0 {
   788			return false // No files tracked = no overlap evidence
   789		}
   790		// Only check files that were actually changed in this commit.
   791		// Without this, files that exist in the tree but weren't changed
   792		// would pass the "modified file" check in filesOverlapWithContent
   793		// (because the file exists in the parent tree), causing stale
   794		// sessions to be incorrectly condensed.
   795		var committedTouchedFiles []string
   796		for _, f := range h.filesTouchedBefore {
   797			if _, ok := h.committedFileSet[f]; ok {
   798				committedTouchedFiles = append(committedTouchedFiles, f)
   799			}
   800		}
   801		if len(committedTouchedFiles) == 0 {
   802			return false
   803		}
   804		return filesOverlapWithContent(h.ctx, h.repo, h.shadowBranchName, h.commit, committedTouchedFiles, overlapOpts{
   805			headTree:      h.headTree,
   806			shadowTree:    h.shadowTree,
   807			parentTree:    h.parentTree,
   808			hasParentTree: true,
   809		})
   810	}

   812	const (
   813		staleEndedSessionWarnThreshold = 3                   // warn when ≥ this many stale sessions
   814		staleEndedSessionWarnInterval  = 24 * time.Hour      // rate-limit window
   815		staleEndedSessionWarnFile      = ".warn-stale-ended" // sentinel file name in entire-sessions/
   816	)
   817	
   818	// stderrWriter is the destination for user-facing warnings emitted outside of
   819	// Cobra command output (e.g. from PostCommit). Tests can swap this to capture
   820	// output without mutating the process-global os.Stderr.
   821	var stderrWriter io.Writer = os.Stderr
   822	
   823	// warnStaleEndedSessions emits a rate-limited warning to stderr when too many
   824	// non-FullyCondensed ENDED sessions are accumulating.
   825	func warnStaleEndedSessions(ctx context.Context, count int) {
   826		warnStaleEndedSessionsTo(ctx, count, stderrWriter)
   827	}
   828	
   829	func warnStaleEndedSessionsTo(ctx context.Context, count int, w io.Writer) {
   830		root, err := gitdir.Open(ctx)
   831		if err != nil {
   832			return // fail-open
   833		}
   834		warnFile := session.SessionStateDirName + "/" + staleEndedSessionWarnFile
   835		if info, statErr := root.Lstat(warnFile); statErr == nil {
   836			if time.Since(info.ModTime()) < staleEndedSessionWarnInterval {
   837				return // rate-limited
   838			}
   839		}
   840		//nolint:errcheck // Best-effort warning — fail-open if file ops fail
   841		_ = osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink(root, session.SessionStateDirName, 0o750)
   842		//nolint:errcheck // Best-effort sentinel file write
   843		_ = jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn(root, warnFile, []byte{}, 0o644)
   844		fmt.Fprintf(w,
   845			"\nentire: %d ended session(s) are accumulating and slowing down commits.\n"+
   846				"Run 'entire doctor' to condense them and restore commit performance.\n\n",
   847			count,
   848		)
   849	}

   187	var trailerLineRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*: `)
   188	
   189	// IsTrailerLine reports whether a line matches git trailer format.
   190	func IsTrailerLine(line string) bool {
   191		return trailerLineRe.MatchString(line)
   192	}
   193	
   194	// appendTrailerLine appends a single pre-formatted trailer line (e.g. "Key: value")
   195	// to message in trailer-block-aware format. If the message already ends with a
   196	// trailer paragraph the line is joined directly to it; otherwise a blank line is
   197	// inserted first to start a new trailer block.
   198	func appendTrailerLine(message, trailerLine string) string {
   199		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(message, "\n")
   200	
   201		lines := strings.Split(trimmed, "\n")
   202		i := len(lines) - 1
   203		for i >= 0 && strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]), "#") {
   204			i--
   205		}
   206	
   207		hasTrailerBlock := false
   208		if i >= 0 {
   209			last := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   210			if last != "" && IsTrailerLine(last) {
   211				for i > 0 {
   212					i--
   213					above := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   214					if strings.HasPrefix(above, "#") {
   215						continue
   216					}
   217					if above == "" {
   218						hasTrailerBlock = true
   219						break
   220					}
   221					if !IsTrailerLine(above) {
   222						break
   223					}
   224				}
   225			}
   226		}
   227	
   228		if hasTrailerBlock {
   229			return trimmed + "\n" + trailerLine + "\n"
   230		}
   231		return trimmed + "\n\n" + trailerLine + "\n"
   232	}

   244	// treated as "OPF not applied" so the pre-push rewrite considers the
   245	// commit a candidate for OPF redaction. Pinning the value to literal

   249	func HasOPFApplied(commitMessage string) bool {

   272		}
   273		end := i + 1

   275			i--
   276		}
   277		start := i + 1
   278		if start == end {

   280		}
   281		if i >= 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]) != "" {

   283		}
   284		return lines[start:end]

   295		}

   298	}

   194	// appendTrailerLine appends a single pre-formatted trailer line (e.g. "Key: value")
   195	// to message in trailer-block-aware format. If the message already ends with a
   196	// trailer paragraph the line is joined directly to it; otherwise a blank line is
   197	// inserted first to start a new trailer block.
   198	func appendTrailerLine(message, trailerLine string) string {
   199		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(message, "\n")
   200	
   201		lines := strings.Split(trimmed, "\n")
   202		i := len(lines) - 1
   203		for i >= 0 && strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]), "#") {
   204			i--
   205		}
   206	
   207		hasTrailerBlock := false
   208		if i >= 0 {
   209			last := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   210			if last != "" && IsTrailerLine(last) {
   211				for i > 0 {
   212					i--
   213					above := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   214					if strings.HasPrefix(above, "#") {
   215						continue
   216					}
   217					if above == "" {
   218						hasTrailerBlock = true
   219						break
   220					}
   221					if !IsTrailerLine(above) {
   222						break
   223					}
   224				}
   225			}
   226		}
   227	
   228		if hasTrailerBlock {
   229			return trimmed + "\n" + trailerLine + "\n"
   230		}
   231		return trimmed + "\n\n" + trailerLine + "\n"
   232	}

   242	// HasOPFApplied reports whether the commit message carries an
   243	// `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer. Any other value (or absence) is
   244	// treated as "OPF not applied" so the pre-push rewrite considers the
   245	// commit a candidate for OPF redaction. Pinning the value to literal
   246	// "true" — rather than just trailer presence — prevents a future
   247	// "Entire-OPF-Applied: false" or "skipped" from accidentally meaning
   248	// "yes, applied."
   249	func HasOPFApplied(commitMessage string) bool {
   250		for _, line := range finalTrailerBlock(commitMessage) {
   251			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
   252			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, ":")
   253			if !ok || key != OPFAppliedTrailerKey {
   254				continue
   255			}
   256			if strings.TrimSpace(value) == OPFAppliedTrailerValue {
   257				return true
   258			}
   259		}
   260		return false
   261	}

   263	func finalTrailerBlock(message string) []string {
   264		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(message, "\n")
   265		if trimmed == "" {
   266			return nil
   267		}
   268		lines := strings.Split(trimmed, "\n")
   269		i := len(lines) - 1
   270		for i >= 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]) == "" {
   271			i--
   272		}
   273		end := i + 1
   274		for i >= 0 && IsTrailerLine(strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])) {
   275			i--
   276		}
   277		start := i + 1
   278		if start == end {
   279			return nil
   280		}
   281		if i >= 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[i]) != "" {
   282			return nil
   283		}
   284		return lines[start:end]
   285	}

   287	// AppendOPFAppliedTrailer appends `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` in
   288	// trailer-aware format. Idempotent: if the message already carries

   290	// unchanged so re-parenting an already-applied commit doesn't

   292	func AppendOPFAppliedTrailer(message string) string {

   295		}
   296		trailer := fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", OPFAppliedTrailerKey, OPFAppliedTrailerValue)
   297		return appendTrailerLine(message, trailer)
   298	}

    58	// writeSession writes a committed checkpoint to the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.

    63	func (s *GitStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {

    66		// expensive write there is. Nothing below here observes cancellation

    69		// checkpoints after Ctrl-C.

   112	// subtreeObjAt returns the tree object for one checkpoint's subtree within a root
   113	// tree, or (nil, nil) when the root or the checkpoint path does not exist yet.
   114	// path is the in-tree checkpoint path (e.g. "a3/b2c4d5e6f7"); pass "" to return
   115	// the root tree itself (the per-checkpoint-ref layout, where the whole tree is
   116	// the checkpoint subtree).
   117	func (s *treeWriter) subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, path string) (*object.Tree, error) {
   118		if rootTreeHash == plumbing.ZeroHash {
   119			return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // absent checkpoint (no tree yet), not an error
   120		}
   121		rootTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(rootTreeHash)

   138	// checkpointSubtreePath joins a checkpoint-relative git tree path from a base and
   139	// trailing segments using path.Join. Git tree paths are always "/"-separated, so
   140	// this uses the stdlib path package (never path/filepath, which would emit "\" on
   141	// Windows and corrupt tree keys). path.Join cleans separators, so base may be ""
   142	// (per-checkpoint-ref root), a clean dir ("a3/b2.../0"), or a trailing-slash dir
   143	// ("a3/b2.../"): checkpointSubtreePath("", "0", "metadata.json") == "0/metadata.json"
   144	// and checkpointSubtreePath("a3/b2.../", "0", "metadata.json") == "a3/b2.../0/metadata.json".
   145	// Callers therefore need not maintain the trailing-slash invariant by hand.
   146	func checkpointSubtreePath(base string, segs ...string) string {
   147		if len(segs) == 0 {
   148			// path.Join with no segments would clean a "" base to "." — an invalid
   149			// git tree key. At the ref root the correct key is ""; for a non-empty
   150			// base, clean it to keep the trailing-slash-stripping behavior.
   151			if base == "" {
   152				return ""
   153			}
   154			return path.Clean(base)
   155		}
   156		return path.Join(append([]string{base}, segs...)...)
   157	}

    58	// writeSession writes a committed checkpoint to the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.

    63	func (s *GitStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {

    65		// canceled ctx means stop doing work, and creating a checkpoint is the most
    66		// expensive write there is. Nothing below here observes cancellation

    68		// without this a bulk writer that ignores cancellation keeps minting
    69		// checkpoints after Ctrl-C.

    72		}

   112	// subtreeObjAt returns the tree object for one checkpoint's subtree within a root
   113	// tree, or (nil, nil) when the root or the checkpoint path does not exist yet.
   114	// path is the in-tree checkpoint path (e.g. "a3/b2c4d5e6f7"); pass "" to return
   115	// the root tree itself (the per-checkpoint-ref layout, where the whole tree is
   116	// the checkpoint subtree).
   117	func (s *treeWriter) subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, path string) (*object.Tree, error) {
   118		if rootTreeHash == plumbing.ZeroHash {
   119			return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // absent checkpoint (no tree yet), not an error
   120		}
   121		rootTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(rootTreeHash)

   126			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read root tree %s: %w", rootTreeHash, err)

   138	// checkpointSubtreePath joins a checkpoint-relative git tree path from a base and
   139	// trailing segments using path.Join. Git tree paths are always "/"-separated, so
   140	// this uses the stdlib path package (never path/filepath, which would emit "\" on
   141	// Windows and corrupt tree keys). path.Join cleans separators, so base may be ""
   142	// (per-checkpoint-ref root), a clean dir ("a3/b2.../0"), or a trailing-slash dir
   143	// ("a3/b2.../"): checkpointSubtreePath("", "0", "metadata.json") == "0/metadata.json"
   144	// and checkpointSubtreePath("a3/b2.../", "0", "metadata.json") == "a3/b2.../0/metadata.json".
   145	// Callers therefore need not maintain the trailing-slash invariant by hand.
   146	func checkpointSubtreePath(base string, segs ...string) string {
   147		if len(segs) == 0 {
   148			// path.Join with no segments would clean a "" base to "." — an invalid
   149			// git tree key. At the ref root the correct key is ""; for a non-empty
   150			// base, clean it to keep the trailing-slash-stripping behavior.
   151			if base == "" {
   152				return ""
   153			}
   154			return path.Clean(base)
   155		}

   648	func (s *treeWriter) writeSessionToSubdirectory(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions, sessionDir string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (SessionFilePaths, error) {

   138	// checkpointSubtreePath joins a checkpoint-relative git tree path from a base and
   139	// trailing segments using path.Join. Git tree paths are always "/"-separated, so

   141	// Windows and corrupt tree keys). path.Join cleans separators, so base may be ""
   142	// (per-checkpoint-ref root), a clean dir ("a3/b2.../0"), or a trailing-slash dir
   143	// ("a3/b2.../"): checkpointSubtreePath("", "0", "metadata.json") == "0/metadata.json"
   144	// and checkpointSubtreePath("a3/b2.../", "0", "metadata.json") == "a3/b2.../0/metadata.json".

   146	func checkpointSubtreePath(base string, segs ...string) string {

   149			// git tree key. At the ref root the correct key is ""; for a non-empty

   112	// subtreeObjAt returns the tree object for one checkpoint's subtree within a root

   117	func (s *treeWriter) subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash plumbing.Hash, path string) (*object.Tree, error) {

   138	// checkpointSubtreePath joins a checkpoint-relative git tree path from a base and
   139	// trailing segments using path.Join. Git tree paths are always "/"-separated, so
   140	// this uses the stdlib path package (never path/filepath, which would emit "\" on
   141	// Windows and corrupt tree keys). path.Join cleans separators, so base may be ""
   142	// (per-checkpoint-ref root), a clean dir ("a3/b2.../0"), or a trailing-slash dir
   143	// ("a3/b2.../"): checkpointSubtreePath("", "0", "metadata.json") == "0/metadata.json"
   144	// and checkpointSubtreePath("a3/b2.../", "0", "metadata.json") == "a3/b2.../0/metadata.json".

   400			// of this operation, remembered so the outage is paid once.
   401			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: skipped, an earlier checkpoint-ref fetch already failed in this operation: %w", refName, priorFailure)

   407				// failure, and per-ref, so it is not memoized.

   413			// CALLER's context says nothing about the remote and must not poison
   414			// later fetches on this store.
   415			if ctx.Err() == nil {

   425		}

   427		// remote genuinely has no such checkpoint; anything else is a real error.

   493	// List enumerates local checkpoint refs and reads each root summary, sorted most
   494	// recent first.
   495	//
   496	// When the context opts in (WithRemoteListDiscovery) and a remote ref lister is
   497	// configured, it additionally discovers checkpoints that exist on the
   498	// checkpoint remote but have no local ref yet — the "second device sees zero
   499	// checkpoints" case. Discovery is names-only (an ls-remote of
   500	// refs/entire/checkpoints/*, no object transfer): each remote-only checkpoint is
   501	// listed from its ref name alone and hydrated lazily on a later read via the
   502	// on-demand ref fetch. Remote enumeration is best-effort and additive — a
   503	// failure logs and leaves the local results intact rather than failing the
   504	// whole listing.
   505	func (s *gitRefsStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]CheckpointInfo, error) {
   506		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   507			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   508		}

   528			if treeErr != nil {
   529				return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable refs, keep listing
   530			}

   532			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   533			return nil
   534		})
   535		if err != nil {
   536			return nil, fmt.Errorf("iterate checkpoint refs: %w", err)
   537		}

   540			checkpoints = s.appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx, checkpoints, seen)
   541		}

   547	// appendRemoteDiscovered enumerates checkpoint refs on the configured checkpoint
   548	// remote and appends any that are not present locally (tracked in seen) as
   549	// not-yet-hydrated CheckpointInfos. It never fetches objects: the ref name
   550	// yields the checkpoint ID, and a ULID ID yields its creation time, so a
   551	// discovered checkpoint sorts and displays correctly before its first read
   552	// hydrates the rest. Best-effort: an enumeration failure logs, warns on stderr,
   553	// and returns the unchanged local list.
   554	func (s *gitRefsStore) appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx context.Context, checkpoints []CheckpointInfo, seen map[id.CheckpointID]struct{}) []CheckpointInfo {
   555		remoteRefs, err := s.remoteRefLister(ctx)
   556		if err != nil {
   557			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote checkpoint enumeration failed; listing local refs only",
   558				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   559			// Match WarnIfMetadataDisconnected: opted-in discovery failing must be
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   561			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: could not reach checkpoint remote; showing local checkpoints only.")

   563		}
   564		for _, refName := range remoteRefs {
   565			cid, ok := ParseRef(refName)
   566			if !ok {
   567				continue
   568			}
   569			if _, dup := seen[cid]; dup {
   570				continue
   571			}
   572			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   573			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid))
   574		}
   575		return checkpoints

   578	// remoteDiscoveredInfo builds the minimal CheckpointInfo for a checkpoint known
   579	// only by its remote ref name. Its contents are not fetched here (that happens
   580	// lazily on read); CreatedAt is recovered from the ULID timestamp so the entry
   581	// sorts by real creation time, and is left zero for a (rare) legacy-hex ref.
   582	// ListedStub marks the entry so hydration can distinguish it from a local ref
   583	// whose root metadata was unreadable (same zero SessionID/SessionCount shape).
   584	func remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid id.CheckpointID) CheckpointInfo {
   585		info := CheckpointInfo{CheckpointID: cid, ListedStub: true}
   586		if createdAt, ok := cid.Time(); ok {
   587			info.CreatedAt = createdAt
   588		}
   589		return info
   590	}
   591	
   592	// listedCheckpointNeedsHydration reports whether info is a names-only List stub
   593	// that still needs a hydrate attempt. It keys off ListedStub (set by
   594	// remoteDiscoveredInfo), not SessionID/SessionCount zero-ness: a local ref whose
   595	// root metadata.json is missing/unreadable has the same zero fields but must not
   596	// be treated as a stub (hydration can never fix it and would re-fetch forever).
   597	// Callers that need session identity for filtering or display should
   598	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo first.
   599	func listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info CheckpointInfo) bool {
   600		return info.ListedStub && !info.CheckpointID.IsEmpty()
   601	}
   602	
   603	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo fills SessionID/Agent/etc for a List entry that
   604	// was discovered by name only. It reads the checkpoint (triggering an on-demand
   605	// ref fetch when configured) and mirrors the fields List populates for local
   606	// refs via readCommittedInfoFromCheckpointTree, with one deliberate CreatedAt
   607	// divergence: the local List path assigns info.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   608	// unconditionally, while hydration only overwrites when meta.CreatedAt is
   609	// non-zero (keeping the ULID-derived time from remoteDiscoveredInfo).
   610	//
   611	// Best-effort / fail-once: on Read or last-session metadata failure it logs Warn,
   612	// clears ListedStub so callers do not re-fetch, and returns the original stub
   613	// fields (never a half-hydrated SessionCount-without-SessionID that would poison
   614	// a committedByID cache and still look "done").
   615	func HydrateListedCheckpointInfo(ctx context.Context, store interface {
   616		Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error)
   617		ReadSessionMetadata(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*Metadata, error)
   618	}, info CheckpointInfo) CheckpointInfo {
   619		if !listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info) {
   620			return info
   621		}
   622		summary, err := store.Read(ctx, info.CheckpointID)
   623		if err != nil || summary == nil {
   624			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to hydrate remote-discovered checkpoint; leaving stub without session metadata",
   625				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   626				slog.String("error", errString(err)))
   627			info.ListedStub = false // fail-once: do not re-fetch on every list
   628			return info
   629		}
   630	
   631		out := info
   632		out.ListedStub = false
   633		out.CheckpointsCount = summary.CheckpointsCount
   634		out.FilesTouched = summary.FilesTouched
   635		out.SessionCount = len(summary.Sessions)
   636		out.Imported = summary.Imported
   637		out.SessionIDs = nil
   638		lastMetaOK := len(summary.Sessions) == 0
   639		for i := range summary.Sessions {
   640			meta, metaErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, info.CheckpointID, i)
   641			if metaErr != nil || meta == nil {
   642				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to read session metadata while hydrating remote-discovered checkpoint",
   643					slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   644					slog.Int("session_index", i),
   645					slog.String("error", errString(metaErr)))
   646				continue
   647			}
   648			if meta.SessionID != "" {
   649				out.SessionIDs = append(out.SessionIDs, meta.SessionID)
   650			}
   651			if i == len(summary.Sessions)-1 {
   652				out.Agent = meta.Agent
   653				out.SessionID = meta.SessionID
   654				if !meta.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
   655					out.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   656				}
   657				out.IsTask = meta.IsTask
   658				out.ToolUseID = meta.ToolUseID
   659				lastMetaOK = true
   660			}
   661		}
   662		if !lastMetaOK {
   663			// Avoid caching SessionCount>0 with empty SessionID: that shape no longer
   664			// needs hydration under the old zero-field heuristic and would poison
   665			// committedByID / --session filters. Fail-once on the original stub.
   666			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote-discovered checkpoint hydration incomplete; leaving stub without session metadata",
   667				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()))
   668			info.ListedStub = false
   669			return info
   670		}
   671		return out
   672	}

   676			return "nil result"
   677		}

   681	// GetCheckpointAuthor returns the author of the checkpoint ref's tip commit (the
   682	// most recent writer). Returns a zero Author when the ref is absent.
   683	func (s *gitRefsStore) GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (Author, error) {
   684		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   685			return Author{}, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   686		}
   687		refName, err := RefName(checkpointID)
   688		if err != nil {
   689			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // invalid ID → unknown author
   690		}
   691		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   692		if err != nil {
   693			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // no ref → unknown author
   694		}
   695		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   696		if err != nil {
   697			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // unreadable → unknown author
   698		}
   699		return Author{Name: commit.Author.Name, Email: commit.Author.Email}, nil

    39	// gitRefsStore is the git-backed persistent checkpoint store that keeps one ref
    40	// per checkpoint at refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>. Each ref points at a
    41	// commit whose tree root IS that checkpoint's contents (metadata.json, 0/, 1/,
    42	// tasks/…), so updates advance the ref and preserve per-checkpoint history. It

    44	// embedded *treeWriter (anchored at basePath ""), differing only in where the
    45	// subtree is committed: a per-checkpoint ref instead of the v1 branch.

    49		blobFetcher     BlobFetchFunc

    56		// or too-slow-for-the-budget — network once instead of N times. Genuine
    57		// remote absence is per-ref and

   132	// refBase resolves a checkpoint ref's current tip commit (the parent for the
   133	// next write) and subtree object (the checkpoint's current contents) with a
   134	// LOCAL-ONLY lookup. A missing ref yields (ZeroHash, nil) so the next write
   135	// becomes an orphan commit — correct for creates, whose ref never exists yet
   136	// (locally or remotely); probing the remote would add a doomed round-trip to
   137	// every condensation and, with a fetcher configured, fail offline writes.
   138	// Backfills, which target an existing checkpoint, use refBaseForBackfill
   139	// instead. Migration (migrate.go) also uses refBase deliberately: it imports

   142	// existing checkpoint — attach, which adds a session to it — but attach
   143	// pre-fetches and verifies the ref's presence itself (refreshCheckpoint)
   144	// before writing, so the local-only probe is safe there too.
   145	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBase(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {

   186	// refTip reads the commit and tree at a resolved checkpoint ref.
   187	func (s *gitRefsStore) refTip(cid id.CheckpointID, ref *plumbing.Reference) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   188		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s: %w", ref.Hash(), err)
   191		}
   192		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   193		if err != nil {
   194			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   195		}
   196		return ref.Hash(), tree, nil
   197	}

   199	// enqueueForPush records refName in the push-discovery queue, logging (never
   200	// returning) on failure so the local ref write still succeeds.
   201	//
   202	// The queue is resolved with the cancellation stripped from ctx. By the time we
   203	// get here the ref is already written locally, and the queue is the ONLY
   204	// push-discovery mechanism there is — see the
   205	// pushQueueFileName doc. A ref that misses the queue is never pushed, and the
   206	// writers above are idempotent, so a re-run skips it as already-present and
   207	// never re-enqueues it: it stays local-only forever. Resolving the queue shells
   208	// out to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which fails instantly on a canceled
   209	// ctx, so honoring cancellation here would drop the bookkeeping for a write
   210	// that already happened. This local, sub-millisecond step therefore completes
   211	// even during shutdown (a second Ctrl-C still force-quits the process).
   212	func (s *gitRefsStore) enqueueForPush(ctx context.Context, refName plumbing.ReferenceName) {
   213		q, err := PushQueueForRepo(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), s.repo)
   214		if err != nil {
   215			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: resolve push queue failed; ref not enqueued",
   216				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   217			return
   218		}
   219		if err := q.Enqueue(refName); err != nil {
   220			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed",
   221				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   222		}
   223	}

   225	func (s *gitRefsStore) updateCheckpointRef(
   226		ctx context.Context,
   227		cid id.CheckpointID,
   228		base func() (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error),
   229		build func(parentHash plumbing.Hash, existing *object.Tree) (plumbing.Hash, error),
   230	) error {
   231		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   232		if err != nil {
   233			return err
   234		}
   235		err = updatePersistentRef(ctx, s.repo, refName, func() (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   236			parentHash, existing, baseErr := base()
   237			if baseErr != nil {
   238				return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, baseErr
   239			}
   240			newHash, buildErr := build(parentHash, existing)
   241			return newHash, parentHash, buildErr
   242		})
   243		if err != nil {
   244			return err
   245		}
   246		s.enqueueForPush(ctx, refName)
   247		return nil
   248	}

   250	func (s *gitRefsStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {
   251		// Parity with the backfill writers above and with GitStore.writeSession: a
   252		// canceled ctx means stop doing work, and creating a checkpoint is the most
   253		// expensive write there is (tree building plus a commit). Without this a
   254		// bulk writer that ignores cancellation — `entire import` was one — keeps
   255		// minting checkpoints after Ctrl-C.
   256		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   257			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   258		}
   259		if opts.CheckpointID.IsEmpty() {
   260			return errors.New("invalid checkpoint options: checkpoint ID is required")
   261		}
   262		if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
   263			return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
   264		}
   265		return s.updateCheckpointRef(ctx, opts.CheckpointID,
   266			func() (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   267				return s.refBase(opts.CheckpointID)
   268			},
   269			func(parentHash plumbing.Hash, existing *object.Tree) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   270				checkpointSubtree, err := s.applySessionWrite(ctx, opts, existing, "")
   271				if err != nil {
   272					return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   273				}
   274				commitMsg := s.buildCommitMessage(opts)
   275				return CreateCommit(ctx, s.repo, checkpointSubtree, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
   276			},
   277		)
   278	}

   346	// checkpointTree resolves a FetchingTree rooted at a checkpoint's ref commit
   347	// tree (which is the checkpoint subtree itself). Returns ErrCheckpointNotFound
   348	// when the ref or its commit/tree cannot be resolved.
   349	func (s *gitRefsStore) checkpointTree(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*FetchingTree, error) {
   350		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   351			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   352		}
   353		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   354		if err != nil {
   355			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   356				return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   357			}
   358			return nil, err
   359		}
   360		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   361		if err != nil {
   362			// The ref resolved but its commit object doesn't — corruption/IO, not an
   363			// absent checkpoint. Surface it instead of masking as "not found".
   364			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s for %s: %w", ref.Hash(), cid, err)
   365		}
   366		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   367		if err != nil {
   368			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   369		}
   370		return NewFetchingTree(ctx, tree, s.repo.Storer, s.blobFetcher), nil
   371	}
   372	
   373	// resolveRefMaybeFetch resolves a checkpoint ref, fetching it from the remote
   374	// once when it is missing locally and a ref fetcher is configured (the
   375	// checkpoint may have been written on another machine). It distinguishes a
   376	// genuinely absent ref (returns a plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound-wrapped error,
   377	// which callers map to ErrCheckpointNotFound) from a real failure — an IO error,
   378	// or a fetch that failed for network/context reasons — which is returned as-is
   379	// so it is not silently swallowed as "checkpoint not found".
   380	func (s *gitRefsStore) resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*plumbing.Reference, error) {
   381		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   382		if err != nil {
   383			return nil, err
   384		}
   385		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   386		if err == nil {
   387			return ref, nil
   388		}
   389		if !errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   390			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   391		}
   392		if s.refFetcher == nil {
   393			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // genuinely absent; caller maps ErrReferenceNotFound to ErrCheckpointNotFound
   394		}
   395		s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   396		priorFailure := s.fetchFailure
   397		s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   398		if priorFailure != nil {
   399			// Note the cause may name a DIFFERENT ref — it is the first failure
   400			// of this operation, remembered so the outage is paid once.
   401			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: skipped, an earlier checkpoint-ref fetch already failed in this operation: %w", refName, priorFailure)
   402		}
   403		if fetchErr := s.refFetcher(ctx, refName); fetchErr != nil {
   404			if errors.Is(fetchErr, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   405				// The fetcher probed the remote and it genuinely lacks this ref
   406				// (remote.FetchCheckpointRef's absence signal) — absence, not a
   407				// failure, and per-ref, so it is not memoized.
   408				logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: remote has no such checkpoint ref",
   409					slog.String("ref", refName.String()))
   410				return nil, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound
   411			}
   412			// Memoize only network verdicts: a cancellation originating from the
   413			// CALLER's context says nothing about the remote and must not poison
   414			// later fetches on this store.
   415			if ctx.Err() == nil {
   416				s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   417				if s.fetchFailure == nil {
   418					s.fetchFailure = fetchErr
   419				}
   420				s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   421			}
   422			logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: on-demand checkpoint ref fetch failed",
   423				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()))
   424			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, fetchErr)
   425		}
   426		// Re-resolve after a successful fetch. ErrReferenceNotFound here means the
   427		// remote genuinely has no such checkpoint; anything else is a real error.
   428		ref, err = s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   429		if err != nil {
   430			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ErrReferenceNotFound (absent) or a real error; caller distinguishes via errors.Is
   431		}
   432		return ref, nil
   433	}

   493	// List enumerates local checkpoint refs and reads each root summary, sorted most
   494	// recent first.
   495	//
   496	// When the context opts in (WithRemoteListDiscovery) and a remote ref lister is
   497	// configured, it additionally discovers checkpoints that exist on the
   498	// checkpoint remote but have no local ref yet — the "second device sees zero
   499	// checkpoints" case. Discovery is names-only (an ls-remote of
   500	// refs/entire/checkpoints/*, no object transfer): each remote-only checkpoint is
   501	// listed from its ref name alone and hydrated lazily on a later read via the
   502	// on-demand ref fetch. Remote enumeration is best-effort and additive — a
   503	// failure logs and leaves the local results intact rather than failing the
   504	// whole listing.
   505	func (s *gitRefsStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]CheckpointInfo, error) {
   506		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   507			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   508		}
   509	
   510		refs, err := s.repo.References()
   511		if err != nil {
   512			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list checkpoint refs: %w", err)
   513		}
   514		defer refs.Close()
   515	
   516		var checkpoints []CheckpointInfo
   517		seen := make(map[id.CheckpointID]struct{})
   518		err = refs.ForEach(func(ref *plumbing.Reference) error {
   519			cid, ok := ParseRef(ref.Name())
   520			if !ok {
   521				return nil
   522			}
   523			commit, commitErr := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   524			if commitErr != nil {
   525				return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable refs, keep listing
   526			}
   527			tree, treeErr := commit.Tree()
   528			if treeErr != nil {
   529				return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable refs, keep listing
   530			}
   531			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, readCommittedInfoFromCheckpointTree(cid, tree))
   532			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   533			return nil
   534		})
   535		if err != nil {
   536			return nil, fmt.Errorf("iterate checkpoint refs: %w", err)
   537		}
   538	
   539		if s.remoteRefLister != nil && remoteListDiscoveryEnabled(ctx) {
   540			checkpoints = s.appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx, checkpoints, seen)
   541		}
   542	
   543		sortCheckpointInfosByRecency(checkpoints)
   544		return checkpoints, nil
   545	}
   546	
   547	// appendRemoteDiscovered enumerates checkpoint refs on the configured checkpoint
   548	// remote and appends any that are not present locally (tracked in seen) as
   549	// not-yet-hydrated CheckpointInfos. It never fetches objects: the ref name
   550	// yields the checkpoint ID, and a ULID ID yields its creation time, so a
   551	// discovered checkpoint sorts and displays correctly before its first read
   552	// hydrates the rest. Best-effort: an enumeration failure logs, warns on stderr,
   553	// and returns the unchanged local list.
   554	func (s *gitRefsStore) appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx context.Context, checkpoints []CheckpointInfo, seen map[id.CheckpointID]struct{}) []CheckpointInfo {
   555		remoteRefs, err := s.remoteRefLister(ctx)
   556		if err != nil {
   557			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote checkpoint enumeration failed; listing local refs only",
   558				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   559			// Match WarnIfMetadataDisconnected: opted-in discovery failing must be
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   561			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: could not reach checkpoint remote; showing local checkpoints only.")
   562			return checkpoints
   563		}
   564		for _, refName := range remoteRefs {
   565			cid, ok := ParseRef(refName)
   566			if !ok {
   567				continue
   568			}
   569			if _, dup := seen[cid]; dup {
   570				continue
   571			}
   572			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   573			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid))
   574		}
   575		return checkpoints
   576	}
   577	
   578	// remoteDiscoveredInfo builds the minimal CheckpointInfo for a checkpoint known
   579	// only by its remote ref name. Its contents are not fetched here (that happens
   580	// lazily on read); CreatedAt is recovered from the ULID timestamp so the entry
   581	// sorts by real creation time, and is left zero for a (rare) legacy-hex ref.
   582	// ListedStub marks the entry so hydration can distinguish it from a local ref
   583	// whose root metadata was unreadable (same zero SessionID/SessionCount shape).
   584	func remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid id.CheckpointID) CheckpointInfo {
   585		info := CheckpointInfo{CheckpointID: cid, ListedStub: true}
   586		if createdAt, ok := cid.Time(); ok {
   587			info.CreatedAt = createdAt
   588		}
   589		return info
   590	}
   591	
   592	// listedCheckpointNeedsHydration reports whether info is a names-only List stub
   593	// that still needs a hydrate attempt. It keys off ListedStub (set by
   594	// remoteDiscoveredInfo), not SessionID/SessionCount zero-ness: a local ref whose
   595	// root metadata.json is missing/unreadable has the same zero fields but must not
   596	// be treated as a stub (hydration can never fix it and would re-fetch forever).
   597	// Callers that need session identity for filtering or display should
   598	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo first.
   599	func listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info CheckpointInfo) bool {
   600		return info.ListedStub && !info.CheckpointID.IsEmpty()
   601	}
   602	
   603	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo fills SessionID/Agent/etc for a List entry that
   604	// was discovered by name only. It reads the checkpoint (triggering an on-demand
   605	// ref fetch when configured) and mirrors the fields List populates for local
   606	// refs via readCommittedInfoFromCheckpointTree, with one deliberate CreatedAt
   607	// divergence: the local List path assigns info.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   608	// unconditionally, while hydration only overwrites when meta.CreatedAt is
   609	// non-zero (keeping the ULID-derived time from remoteDiscoveredInfo).
   610	//
   611	// Best-effort / fail-once: on Read or last-session metadata failure it logs Warn,
   612	// clears ListedStub so callers do not re-fetch, and returns the original stub
   613	// fields (never a half-hydrated SessionCount-without-SessionID that would poison
   614	// a committedByID cache and still look "done").
   615	func HydrateListedCheckpointInfo(ctx context.Context, store interface {
   616		Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error)
   617		ReadSessionMetadata(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*Metadata, error)
   618	}, info CheckpointInfo) CheckpointInfo {
   619		if !listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info) {
   620			return info
   621		}
   622		summary, err := store.Read(ctx, info.CheckpointID)
   623		if err != nil || summary == nil {
   624			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to hydrate remote-discovered checkpoint; leaving stub without session metadata",
   625				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   626				slog.String("error", errString(err)))
   627			info.ListedStub = false // fail-once: do not re-fetch on every list
   628			return info
   629		}
   630	
   631		out := info
   632		out.ListedStub = false
   633		out.CheckpointsCount = summary.CheckpointsCount
   634		out.FilesTouched = summary.FilesTouched
   635		out.SessionCount = len(summary.Sessions)
   636		out.Imported = summary.Imported
   637		out.SessionIDs = nil
   638		lastMetaOK := len(summary.Sessions) == 0
   639		for i := range summary.Sessions {
   640			meta, metaErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, info.CheckpointID, i)
   641			if metaErr != nil || meta == nil {
   642				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to read session metadata while hydrating remote-discovered checkpoint",
   643					slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   644					slog.Int("session_index", i),
   645					slog.String("error", errString(metaErr)))
   646				continue
   647			}
   648			if meta.SessionID != "" {
   649				out.SessionIDs = append(out.SessionIDs, meta.SessionID)
   650			}
   651			if i == len(summary.Sessions)-1 {
   652				out.Agent = meta.Agent
   653				out.SessionID = meta.SessionID
   654				if !meta.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
   655					out.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   656				}
   657				out.IsTask = meta.IsTask
   658				out.ToolUseID = meta.ToolUseID
   659				lastMetaOK = true
   660			}
   661		}
   662		if !lastMetaOK {
   663			// Avoid caching SessionCount>0 with empty SessionID: that shape no longer
   664			// needs hydration under the old zero-field heuristic and would poison
   665			// committedByID / --session filters. Fail-once on the original stub.
   666			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote-discovered checkpoint hydration incomplete; leaving stub without session metadata",
   667				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()))
   668			info.ListedStub = false
   669			return info
   670		}
   671		return out
   672	}

   681	// GetCheckpointAuthor returns the author of the checkpoint ref's tip commit (the
   682	// most recent writer). Returns a zero Author when the ref is absent.
   683	func (s *gitRefsStore) GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (Author, error) {
   684		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   685			return Author{}, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   686		}
   687		refName, err := RefName(checkpointID)
   688		if err != nil {
   689			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // invalid ID → unknown author
   690		}
   691		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   692		if err != nil {
   693			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // no ref → unknown author
   694		}
   695		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   696		if err != nil {
   697			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // unreadable → unknown author

    39	// gitRefsStore is the git-backed persistent checkpoint store that keeps one ref
    40	// per checkpoint at refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>. Each ref points at a
    41	// commit whose tree root IS that checkpoint's contents (metadata.json, 0/, 1/,
    42	// tasks/…), so updates advance the ref and preserve per-checkpoint history. It
    43	// shares the checkpoint-subtree machinery with the git-branch store via the
    44	// embedded *treeWriter (anchored at basePath ""), differing only in where the
    45	// subtree is committed: a per-checkpoint ref instead of the v1 branch.
    46	type gitRefsStore struct {
    47		*treeWriter
    48	
    49		blobFetcher     BlobFetchFunc
    50		refFetcher      RefFetchFunc
    51		remoteRefLister RemoteRefListFunc
    52	
    53		// fetchFailureMu guards fetchFailure: the first transport-level ref-fetch
    54		// failure, memoized for the store's lifetime so a loop over N missing refs
    55		// (e.g. a stop hook finalizing every checkpoint of a turn) pays a dead —
    56		// or too-slow-for-the-budget — network once instead of N times. Genuine
    57		// remote absence is per-ref and
    58		// is never memoized. The memo never clears — safe because every
    59		// fetcher-wired store today is opened per command/hook invocation; a
    60		// long-lived fetcher-wired store would need an expiry before reusing this.
    61		fetchFailureMu sync.Mutex
    62		fetchFailure   error
    63	}

   113	// Write dispatches a persistent write request to the matching ref operation,
   114	// mirroring the git-branch store's Write.
   115	func (s *gitRefsStore) Write(ctx context.Context, req WriteRequest) error {
   116		switch r := req.(type) {
   117		case Session:
   118			return s.writeSession(ctx, WriteOptions(r))
   119		case ReservedSession:
   120			return s.writeSession(ctx, WriteOptions(r))
   121		case SessionTranscript:
   122			return s.backfillTranscript(ctx, UpdateOptions(r))
   123		case SessionSummary:
   124			return s.backfillSummary(ctx, r.CheckpointID, r.Summary)
   125		case CheckpointAttribution:
   126			return s.backfillAttribution(ctx, r.CheckpointID, r.Attribution)
   127		default:
   128			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint: unsupported write request %T", req)
   129		}
   130	}
   131	
   132	// refBase resolves a checkpoint ref's current tip commit (the parent for the
   133	// next write) and subtree object (the checkpoint's current contents) with a
   134	// LOCAL-ONLY lookup. A missing ref yields (ZeroHash, nil) so the next write
   135	// becomes an orphan commit — correct for creates, whose ref never exists yet
   136	// (locally or remotely); probing the remote would add a doomed round-trip to
   137	// every condensation and, with a fetcher configured, fail offline writes.
   138	// Backfills, which target an existing checkpoint, use refBaseForBackfill
   139	// instead. Migration (migrate.go) also uses refBase deliberately: it imports
   140	// from the LOCAL v1 branch and must never probe the remote, even though its
   141	// target ref may already exist. One writeSession caller does target an
   142	// existing checkpoint — attach, which adds a session to it — but attach
   143	// pre-fetches and verifies the ref's presence itself (refreshCheckpoint)
   144	// before writing, so the local-only probe is safe there too.
   145	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBase(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   146		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   147		if err != nil {
   148			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   149		}
   150		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   151		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   152			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // no ref yet → new checkpoint (orphan)
   153		}
   154		if err != nil {
   155			// A real lookup failure (IO/corruption), not an absent ref: surface it
   156			// rather than silently starting a fresh orphan history over the ref.
   157			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   158		}
   159		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   160	}
   161	
   162	// refBaseForBackfill resolves like refBase, but a ref missing locally is
   163	// first fetched once from the remote (resolveRefMaybeFetch) when a fetcher is
   164	// configured: a backfill targets an EXISTING checkpoint that may have been
   165	// written or migrated on another machine, and declaring it absent without
   166	// looking remotely diverges from the read path — the backfill would be
   167	// handled as targeting a nonexistent checkpoint while reads, which DO fetch,
   168	// serve the refs copy, leaving the backfilled data permanently invisible.
   169	// A ref absent even after the fetch yields (ZeroHash, nil), which the
   170	// backfill helpers report as ErrCheckpointNotFound — the signal that the
   171	// checkpoint does not exist in this backend. A fetch FAILURE is returned
   172	// as-is: transient unavailability must never masquerade as absence, because
   173	// a caller or routing layer acting on a false "absent" would misdirect the
   174	// backfill (e.g. onto a stale copy in another backend) instead of retrying.
   175	func (s *gitRefsStore) refBaseForBackfill(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   176		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   177		if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   178			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, nil // genuinely absent → backfill reports not-found
   179		}
   180		if err != nil {
   181			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, err
   182		}
   183		return s.refTip(cid, ref)
   184	}

   186	// refTip reads the commit and tree at a resolved checkpoint ref.
   187	func (s *gitRefsStore) refTip(cid id.CheckpointID, ref *plumbing.Reference) (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   188		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   189		if err != nil {
   190			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s: %w", ref.Hash(), err)
   191		}
   192		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   193		if err != nil {
   194			return plumbing.ZeroHash, nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   195		}
   196		return ref.Hash(), tree, nil
   197	}

   199	// enqueueForPush records refName in the push-discovery queue, logging (never
   200	// returning) on failure so the local ref write still succeeds.
   201	//
   202	// The queue is resolved with the cancellation stripped from ctx. By the time we
   203	// get here the ref is already written locally, and the queue is the ONLY
   204	// push-discovery mechanism there is — see the
   205	// pushQueueFileName doc. A ref that misses the queue is never pushed, and the
   206	// writers above are idempotent, so a re-run skips it as already-present and
   207	// never re-enqueues it: it stays local-only forever. Resolving the queue shells
   208	// out to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, which fails instantly on a canceled
   209	// ctx, so honoring cancellation here would drop the bookkeeping for a write
   210	// that already happened. This local, sub-millisecond step therefore completes
   211	// even during shutdown (a second Ctrl-C still force-quits the process).
   212	func (s *gitRefsStore) enqueueForPush(ctx context.Context, refName plumbing.ReferenceName) {
   213		q, err := PushQueueForRepo(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), s.repo)
   214		if err != nil {
   215			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: resolve push queue failed; ref not enqueued",
   216				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   217			return
   218		}
   219		if err := q.Enqueue(refName); err != nil {
   220			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed",
   221				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   222		}
   223	}

   225	func (s *gitRefsStore) updateCheckpointRef(
   226		ctx context.Context,
   227		cid id.CheckpointID,

   229		build func(parentHash plumbing.Hash, existing *object.Tree) (plumbing.Hash, error),

   250	func (s *gitRefsStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {
   251		// Parity with the backfill writers above and with GitStore.writeSession: a
   252		// canceled ctx means stop doing work, and creating a checkpoint is the most
   253		// expensive write there is (tree building plus a commit). Without this a
   254		// bulk writer that ignores cancellation — `entire import` was one — keeps
   255		// minting checkpoints after Ctrl-C.
   256		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   257			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   258		}

   260			return errors.New("invalid checkpoint options: checkpoint ID is required")
   261		}
   262		if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(opts.SessionID); err != nil {
   263			return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
   264		}
   265		return s.updateCheckpointRef(ctx, opts.CheckpointID,
   266			func() (plumbing.Hash, *object.Tree, error) {
   267				return s.refBase(opts.CheckpointID)
   268			},
   269			func(parentHash plumbing.Hash, existing *object.Tree) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   270				checkpointSubtree, err := s.applySessionWrite(ctx, opts, existing, "")
   271				if err != nil {

   273				}
   274				commitMsg := s.buildCommitMessage(opts)

   346	// checkpointTree resolves a FetchingTree rooted at a checkpoint's ref commit
   347	// tree (which is the checkpoint subtree itself). Returns ErrCheckpointNotFound
   348	// when the ref or its commit/tree cannot be resolved.
   349	func (s *gitRefsStore) checkpointTree(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*FetchingTree, error) {
   350		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   351			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   352		}
   353		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   354		if err != nil {
   355			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   356				return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   357			}
   358			return nil, err
   359		}
   360		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   361		if err != nil {
   362			// The ref resolved but its commit object doesn't — corruption/IO, not an
   363			// absent checkpoint. Surface it instead of masking as "not found".
   364			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s for %s: %w", ref.Hash(), cid, err)
   365		}
   366		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   367		if err != nil {
   368			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   369		}
   370		return NewFetchingTree(ctx, tree, s.repo.Storer, s.blobFetcher), nil
   371	}
   372	
   373	// resolveRefMaybeFetch resolves a checkpoint ref, fetching it from the remote
   374	// once when it is missing locally and a ref fetcher is configured (the
   375	// checkpoint may have been written on another machine). It distinguishes a
   376	// genuinely absent ref (returns a plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound-wrapped error,
   377	// which callers map to ErrCheckpointNotFound) from a real failure — an IO error,
   378	// or a fetch that failed for network/context reasons — which is returned as-is
   379	// so it is not silently swallowed as "checkpoint not found".
   380	func (s *gitRefsStore) resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*plumbing.Reference, error) {
   381		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   382		if err != nil {
   383			return nil, err
   384		}
   385		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   386		if err == nil {
   387			return ref, nil
   388		}
   389		if !errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   390			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   391		}
   392		if s.refFetcher == nil {
   393			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // genuinely absent; caller maps ErrReferenceNotFound to ErrCheckpointNotFound
   394		}
   395		s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   396		priorFailure := s.fetchFailure
   397		s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   398		if priorFailure != nil {
   399			// Note the cause may name a DIFFERENT ref — it is the first failure
   400			// of this operation, remembered so the outage is paid once.
   401			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: skipped, an earlier checkpoint-ref fetch already failed in this operation: %w", refName, priorFailure)
   402		}
   403		if fetchErr := s.refFetcher(ctx, refName); fetchErr != nil {
   404			if errors.Is(fetchErr, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   405				// The fetcher probed the remote and it genuinely lacks this ref
   406				// (remote.FetchCheckpointRef's absence signal) — absence, not a
   407				// failure, and per-ref, so it is not memoized.
   408				logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: remote has no such checkpoint ref",
   409					slog.String("ref", refName.String()))
   410				return nil, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound
   411			}
   412			// Memoize only network verdicts: a cancellation originating from the
   413			// CALLER's context says nothing about the remote and must not poison
   414			// later fetches on this store.
   415			if ctx.Err() == nil {
   416				s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   417				if s.fetchFailure == nil {
   418					s.fetchFailure = fetchErr
   419				}
   420				s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   421			}
   422			logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: on-demand checkpoint ref fetch failed",
   423				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()))
   424			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, fetchErr)
   425		}
   426		// Re-resolve after a successful fetch. ErrReferenceNotFound here means the
   427		// remote genuinely has no such checkpoint; anything else is a real error.
   428		ref, err = s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   429		if err != nil {
   430			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ErrReferenceNotFound (absent) or a real error; caller distinguishes via errors.Is
   431		}
   432		return ref, nil
   433	}

   346	// checkpointTree resolves a FetchingTree rooted at a checkpoint's ref commit
   347	// tree (which is the checkpoint subtree itself). Returns ErrCheckpointNotFound
   348	// when the ref or its commit/tree cannot be resolved.
   349	func (s *gitRefsStore) checkpointTree(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*FetchingTree, error) {
   350		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   351			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   352		}
   353		ref, err := s.resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx, cid)
   354		if err != nil {
   355			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   356				return nil, ErrCheckpointNotFound
   357			}
   358			return nil, err
   359		}
   360		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   361		if err != nil {
   362			// The ref resolved but its commit object doesn't — corruption/IO, not an
   363			// absent checkpoint. Surface it instead of masking as "not found".
   364			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint commit %s for %s: %w", ref.Hash(), cid, err)
   365		}
   366		tree, err := commit.Tree()
   367		if err != nil {
   368			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read checkpoint tree for %s: %w", cid, err)
   369		}
   370		return NewFetchingTree(ctx, tree, s.repo.Storer, s.blobFetcher), nil
   371	}

   373	// resolveRefMaybeFetch resolves a checkpoint ref, fetching it from the remote
   374	// once when it is missing locally and a ref fetcher is configured (the
   375	// checkpoint may have been written on another machine). It distinguishes a
   376	// genuinely absent ref (returns a plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound-wrapped error,
   377	// which callers map to ErrCheckpointNotFound) from a real failure — an IO error,
   378	// or a fetch that failed for network/context reasons — which is returned as-is
   379	// so it is not silently swallowed as "checkpoint not found".
   380	func (s *gitRefsStore) resolveRefMaybeFetch(ctx context.Context, cid id.CheckpointID) (*plumbing.Reference, error) {
   381		refName, err := RefName(cid)
   382		if err != nil {
   383			return nil, err
   384		}
   385		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   386		if err == nil {
   387			return ref, nil
   388		}
   389		if !errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   390			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, err)
   391		}
   392		if s.refFetcher == nil {
   393			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // genuinely absent; caller maps ErrReferenceNotFound to ErrCheckpointNotFound
   394		}
   395		s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   396		priorFailure := s.fetchFailure
   397		s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   398		if priorFailure != nil {
   399			// Note the cause may name a DIFFERENT ref — it is the first failure
   400			// of this operation, remembered so the outage is paid once.
   401			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: skipped, an earlier checkpoint-ref fetch already failed in this operation: %w", refName, priorFailure)
   402		}
   403		if fetchErr := s.refFetcher(ctx, refName); fetchErr != nil {
   404			if errors.Is(fetchErr, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
   405				// The fetcher probed the remote and it genuinely lacks this ref
   406				// (remote.FetchCheckpointRef's absence signal) — absence, not a
   407				// failure, and per-ref, so it is not memoized.
   408				logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: remote has no such checkpoint ref",
   409					slog.String("ref", refName.String()))
   410				return nil, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound
   411			}
   412			// Memoize only network verdicts: a cancellation originating from the
   413			// CALLER's context says nothing about the remote and must not poison
   414			// later fetches on this store.
   415			if ctx.Err() == nil {
   416				s.fetchFailureMu.Lock()
   417				if s.fetchFailure == nil {
   418					s.fetchFailure = fetchErr
   419				}
   420				s.fetchFailureMu.Unlock()
   421			}
   422			logging.Debug(ctx, "git-refs: on-demand checkpoint ref fetch failed",
   423				slog.String("ref", refName.String()), slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()))
   424			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s: %w", refName, fetchErr)
   425		}
   426		// Re-resolve after a successful fetch. ErrReferenceNotFound here means the
   427		// remote genuinely has no such checkpoint; anything else is a real error.
   428		ref, err = s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   429		if err != nil {
   430			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // ErrReferenceNotFound (absent) or a real error; caller distinguishes via errors.Is
   431		}
   432		return ref, nil
   433	}
