   493	// List enumerates local checkpoint refs and reads each root summary, sorted most
   494	// recent first.
   495	//
   496	// When the context opts in (WithRemoteListDiscovery) and a remote ref lister is
   497	// configured, it additionally discovers checkpoints that exist on the
   498	// checkpoint remote but have no local ref yet — the "second device sees zero
   499	// checkpoints" case. Discovery is names-only (an ls-remote of
   500	// refs/entire/checkpoints/*, no object transfer): each remote-only checkpoint is
   501	// listed from its ref name alone and hydrated lazily on a later read via the
   502	// on-demand ref fetch. Remote enumeration is best-effort and additive — a
   503	// failure logs and leaves the local results intact rather than failing the
   504	// whole listing.
   505	func (s *gitRefsStore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]CheckpointInfo, error) {
   506		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   507			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   508		}
   509	
   510		refs, err := s.repo.References()
   511		if err != nil {
   512			return nil, fmt.Errorf("list checkpoint refs: %w", err)
   513		}
   514		defer refs.Close()
   515	
   516		var checkpoints []CheckpointInfo
   517		seen := make(map[id.CheckpointID]struct{})
   518		err = refs.ForEach(func(ref *plumbing.Reference) error {
   519			cid, ok := ParseRef(ref.Name())
   520			if !ok {
   521				return nil
   522			}
   523			commit, commitErr := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   524			if commitErr != nil {
   525				return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable refs, keep listing
   526			}
   527			tree, treeErr := commit.Tree()
   528			if treeErr != nil {
   529				return nil //nolint:nilerr // skip unreadable refs, keep listing
   530			}
   531			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, readCommittedInfoFromCheckpointTree(cid, tree))
   532			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   533			return nil
   534		})
   535		if err != nil {
   536			return nil, fmt.Errorf("iterate checkpoint refs: %w", err)
   537		}
   538	
   539		if s.remoteRefLister != nil && remoteListDiscoveryEnabled(ctx) {
   540			checkpoints = s.appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx, checkpoints, seen)
   541		}
   542	
   543		sortCheckpointInfosByRecency(checkpoints)
   544		return checkpoints, nil
   545	}
   546	
   547	// appendRemoteDiscovered enumerates checkpoint refs on the configured checkpoint
   548	// remote and appends any that are not present locally (tracked in seen) as
   549	// not-yet-hydrated CheckpointInfos. It never fetches objects: the ref name
   550	// yields the checkpoint ID, and a ULID ID yields its creation time, so a
   551	// discovered checkpoint sorts and displays correctly before its first read
   552	// hydrates the rest. Best-effort: an enumeration failure logs, warns on stderr,
   553	// and returns the unchanged local list.
   554	func (s *gitRefsStore) appendRemoteDiscovered(ctx context.Context, checkpoints []CheckpointInfo, seen map[id.CheckpointID]struct{}) []CheckpointInfo {
   555		remoteRefs, err := s.remoteRefLister(ctx)
   556		if err != nil {
   557			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote checkpoint enumeration failed; listing local refs only",
   558				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   559			// Match WarnIfMetadataDisconnected: opted-in discovery failing must be
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   560			// visible on stderr — logging.Warn alone lands only in .entire/logs/.
   561			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: could not reach checkpoint remote; showing local checkpoints only.")
   562			return checkpoints
   563		}
   564		for _, refName := range remoteRefs {
   565			cid, ok := ParseRef(refName)
   566			if !ok {
   567				continue
   568			}
   569			if _, dup := seen[cid]; dup {
   570				continue
   571			}
   572			seen[cid] = struct{}{}
   573			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid))
   574		}
   575		return checkpoints
   576	}
   577	
   578	// remoteDiscoveredInfo builds the minimal CheckpointInfo for a checkpoint known
   579	// only by its remote ref name. Its contents are not fetched here (that happens
   580	// lazily on read); CreatedAt is recovered from the ULID timestamp so the entry
   581	// sorts by real creation time, and is left zero for a (rare) legacy-hex ref.
   582	// ListedStub marks the entry so hydration can distinguish it from a local ref
   583	// whose root metadata was unreadable (same zero SessionID/SessionCount shape).
   584	func remoteDiscoveredInfo(cid id.CheckpointID) CheckpointInfo {
   585		info := CheckpointInfo{CheckpointID: cid, ListedStub: true}
   586		if createdAt, ok := cid.Time(); ok {
   587			info.CreatedAt = createdAt
   588		}
   589		return info
   590	}
   591	
   592	// listedCheckpointNeedsHydration reports whether info is a names-only List stub
   593	// that still needs a hydrate attempt. It keys off ListedStub (set by
   594	// remoteDiscoveredInfo), not SessionID/SessionCount zero-ness: a local ref whose
   595	// root metadata.json is missing/unreadable has the same zero fields but must not
   596	// be treated as a stub (hydration can never fix it and would re-fetch forever).
   597	// Callers that need session identity for filtering or display should
   598	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo first.
   599	func listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info CheckpointInfo) bool {
   600		return info.ListedStub && !info.CheckpointID.IsEmpty()
   601	}
   602	
   603	// HydrateListedCheckpointInfo fills SessionID/Agent/etc for a List entry that
   604	// was discovered by name only. It reads the checkpoint (triggering an on-demand
   605	// ref fetch when configured) and mirrors the fields List populates for local
   606	// refs via readCommittedInfoFromCheckpointTree, with one deliberate CreatedAt
   607	// divergence: the local List path assigns info.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   608	// unconditionally, while hydration only overwrites when meta.CreatedAt is
   609	// non-zero (keeping the ULID-derived time from remoteDiscoveredInfo).
   610	//
   611	// Best-effort / fail-once: on Read or last-session metadata failure it logs Warn,
   612	// clears ListedStub so callers do not re-fetch, and returns the original stub
   613	// fields (never a half-hydrated SessionCount-without-SessionID that would poison
   614	// a committedByID cache and still look "done").
   615	func HydrateListedCheckpointInfo(ctx context.Context, store interface {
   616		Read(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (*CheckpointSummary, error)
   617		ReadSessionMetadata(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionIndex int) (*Metadata, error)
   618	}, info CheckpointInfo) CheckpointInfo {
   619		if !listedCheckpointNeedsHydration(info) {
   620			return info
   621		}
   622		summary, err := store.Read(ctx, info.CheckpointID)
   623		if err != nil || summary == nil {
   624			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to hydrate remote-discovered checkpoint; leaving stub without session metadata",
   625				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   626				slog.String("error", errString(err)))
   627			info.ListedStub = false // fail-once: do not re-fetch on every list
   628			return info
   629		}
   630	
   631		out := info
   632		out.ListedStub = false
   633		out.CheckpointsCount = summary.CheckpointsCount
   634		out.FilesTouched = summary.FilesTouched
   635		out.SessionCount = len(summary.Sessions)
   636		out.Imported = summary.Imported
   637		out.SessionIDs = nil
   638		lastMetaOK := len(summary.Sessions) == 0
   639		for i := range summary.Sessions {
   640			meta, metaErr := store.ReadSessionMetadata(ctx, info.CheckpointID, i)
   641			if metaErr != nil || meta == nil {
   642				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: failed to read session metadata while hydrating remote-discovered checkpoint",
   643					slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()),
   644					slog.Int("session_index", i),
   645					slog.String("error", errString(metaErr)))
   646				continue
   647			}
   648			if meta.SessionID != "" {
   649				out.SessionIDs = append(out.SessionIDs, meta.SessionID)
   650			}
   651			if i == len(summary.Sessions)-1 {
   652				out.Agent = meta.Agent
   653				out.SessionID = meta.SessionID
   654				if !meta.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
   655					out.CreatedAt = meta.CreatedAt
   656				}
   657				out.IsTask = meta.IsTask
   658				out.ToolUseID = meta.ToolUseID
   659				lastMetaOK = true
   660			}
   661		}
   662		if !lastMetaOK {
   663			// Avoid caching SessionCount>0 with empty SessionID: that shape no longer
   664			// needs hydration under the old zero-field heuristic and would poison
   665			// committedByID / --session filters. Fail-once on the original stub.
   666			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs: remote-discovered checkpoint hydration incomplete; leaving stub without session metadata",
   667				slog.String("checkpoint_id", info.CheckpointID.String()))
   668			info.ListedStub = false
   669			return info
   670		}
   671		return out
   672	}

   674	func errString(err error) string {
   675		if err == nil {
   676			return "nil result"
   677		}
   678		return err.Error()
   679	}

   681	// GetCheckpointAuthor returns the author of the checkpoint ref's tip commit (the
   682	// most recent writer). Returns a zero Author when the ref is absent.
   683	func (s *gitRefsStore) GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (Author, error) {
   684		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   685			return Author{}, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
   686		}
   687		refName, err := RefName(checkpointID)
   688		if err != nil {
   689			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // invalid ID → unknown author
   690		}
   691		ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   692		if err != nil {
   693			return Author{}, nil //nolint:nilerr // no ref → unknown author
   694		}
   695		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())

   276	// deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote reports whether publication of the git-branch
   277	// v1 metadata should be held back because the push remote may be brand new.

   280	// repository its default, so the pre-push hook must not publish
   281	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ahead of the user's own first branch. The check is
   282	// purely local: if a remote-tracking ref for this remote already exists
   283	// (refs/remotes/<remote>/*), the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   284	// before and therefore already has at least one branch, so publishing cannot

   286	// remote-tracking ref after the first successful push, so the deferred metadata
   287	// publishes on the next push.

   305		// refs/remotes/<url>/* tracking ref for it — so a tracking-ref check would

   308		// remote.
   309		if !isConfiguredRemote(ctx, ps.remote) {

   314		// over from before a remote was deleted and recreated empty under the same

   318		// recoverable by resetting it on the forge.

   322	// isConfiguredRemote reports whether name is a configured git remote, as

   325	// treated as "not a configured remote".
   326	func isConfiguredRemote(ctx context.Context, name string) bool {
   327		if name == "" {
   328			return false

   331			cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", name)
   332			if worktreeRoot, ok := settings.WorktreeRoot(ctx); ok {
   333				cmd.Dir = worktreeRoot
   334			}
   335			err := cmd.Run()

   337				return true, nil
   338			}

   340			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   340			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   341			// fail-close checkpoint_push_remote for the rest of the process.
   342			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   343			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {

   350	// remoteHasTrackingRefs reports whether any refs/remotes/<remote>/* ref exists

   354	func remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx context.Context, remote string) bool {

   366	// prePushCheckpointRefs drains the per-checkpoint push queue and batch-pushes the
   367	// recorded refs fast-forward-only (git-refs primary; never a force push — a
   368	// diverged ref is recovered via fetch+replay). Transient push failures are logged and

   396		// checkpoint-ref failure must never do that (see this function's doc), so

   398		// refs stay queued, and the user's push proceeds.

   420	// PushQueuedCheckpointRefs pushes any queued checkpoint refs to the configured

   446	// flushCheckpointRefsQueue drains the push-discovery queue and batch-pushes the

   454	func flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ps pushSettings) (int, error) {

   457			return 0, fmt.Errorf("resolve push queue: %w", err)
   458		}
   459		queued, err := queue.Drain()

   461			return 0, fmt.Errorf("drain push queue: %w", err)
   462		}

   465		}

   467		pushCtx, pushSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_checkpoint_refs")

   470		existing, stale := partitionLocalRefs(repo, queued)
   471		if len(stale) > 0 {
   472			if err := queue.Remove(stale); err != nil {
   473				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: prune stale queue entries failed",

   479		}

   481		// Resolved here, not by the caller: it spawns `git remote get-url` and its
   482		// result is unused unless refs are actually pushed, so an ordinary push with
   483		// an empty queue must not pay for it — nor print the multi-URL warning.
   484		dest := resolveRefsPushDestination(pushCtx, ps)

   495		// ref was up to date or fast-forwarded, we're done.
   496		batchErr := batchPushRefs(pushCtx, dest.target, existing)

   502			}
   503			return len(existing), nil
   504		}
   505		stop("")

   508		// fetch+replay. Surface the same actionable hint as the v1 doPushRef path
   509		// (issue #1523) instead of only logging to .entire/logs/.
   510		if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(pushCtx, batchErr) {

   517		}

   519		// At least one ref was rejected — typically a non-fast-forward divergence

   521		// fetch+replay recovery, and remove from the queue only the refs that land
   522		// (a genuine cherry-pick conflict leaves that ref queued for a later push,
   523		// never force-overwriting the remote).
   524		// Deliberately names no cause: the batch fails on divergence, but just as
   525		// often on an unreachable or unauthorized destination. Telling a user with a
   526		// dead remote that their refs "diverged" — or were "rejected", which equally
   527		// implies the remote answered — sends them after the wrong problem.
   528		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Checkpoint ref push failed; retrying %d ref(s) individually...", len(existing))

   532		for _, ref := range existing {
   533			if err := pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(pushCtx, dest.target, ref); err != nil {

   535					slog.String("ref", ref.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))

   538				}

   540					firstErr = err
   541				}

   543			}

   545		}
   546		stop(fmt.Sprintf(" pushed %d of %d", len(pushed), len(existing)))

   548			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: clear pushed refs from queue failed",
   549				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   550		}

   552			return len(pushed), fmt.Errorf("%d of %d checkpoint refs failed to push: %w",
   553				len(existing)-len(pushed), len(existing), firstErr)
   554		}
   555		return len(pushed), nil
   556	}

    66		// Load settings once for remote resolution and push_sessions check.
    67		// Spanned because checkpoint-remote resolution can perform a one-time
    68		// network fetch of the metadata branch (fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing),
    69		// which is otherwise invisible in the pre-push trace.
    70		resolveCtx, resolveSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "resolve_push_settings")
    71		ps := resolvePushSettings(resolveCtx, remote)
    72		resolveSpan.End()
    73	
    74		if ps.pushDisabled {
    75			return nil
    76		}
    77	
    78		// Single-remote gate (ENT-1451): checkpoint data syncs only to the
    79		// elected checkpoint sync remote. A dedicated checkpoint_remote URL is
    80		// exempt — it is a dedicated metadata store addressed directly, not a
    81		// remote selected by this push. The gate must stay BELOW
    82		// resolvePushSettings: hasCheckpointURL is only known after resolution,
    83		// so hoisting the gate above it would break the exemption.
    84		//
    85		// Capture is two-phase, straddling this whole function. The proposal runs
    86		// before the gate so that the push which elects a remote by evidence (push
    87		// target agrees with the branch's declared push destination) is also the
    88		// first push to carry checkpoints there; the election is persisted only at
    89		// the delivery points below, once those checkpoints actually arrived.
    90		// Everything in between can still stop delivery, and the election is
    91		// permanent, so intent is not enough to move it. The hint below then speaks
    92		// only for what capture left gated — see hintGatedCheckpointSync.
    93		var pendingCapture string
    94		if !ps.hasCheckpointURL() {
    95			if pendingCaptureCheckpointSyncRemote(ctx, ps.remote) {
    96				pendingCapture = ps.remote
    97			}
    98			if !checkpointSyncAllowedForRemote(ctx, ps.remote, pendingCapture) {
    99				hintGatedCheckpointSync(ctx, ps.remote)
   100				return nil
   101			}
   102		}
   103	
   104		// git-refs primary: push the per-checkpoint refs recorded in the push queue
   105		// instead of the single v1 branch. Those refs live under refs/entire/, not
   106		// refs/heads/, so a forge can never pick them as a repository's default
   107		// branch — the empty-remote guard below is unnecessary for this backend.
   108		// (A configured git-branch mirror's v1 ref is not pushed here yet — mirror
   109		// push for downgrade safety is a later step.)
   110		if ps.primaryIsRefs {
   111			return s.prePushCheckpointRefs(ctx, ps, pendingCapture)
   112		}
   113	
   114		// git-branch primary: entire/checkpoints/v1 is a real refs/heads branch, so
   115		// on an otherwise-empty remote a forge like GitHub would select it as the
   116		// default. Defer publication until the user's own branch exists there.
   117		deferAutomaticCheckpointPush := protectFirstUserBranch && deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote(ctx, ps)
   118	
   119		refs := checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx)
   120		repo, repoErr := OpenRepository(ctx)
   121		if repoErr != nil {
   122			logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint policy pre-push: failed to open repository; allowing checkpoint push",
   123				slog.String("error", repoErr.Error()),
   124			)
   125		} else {
   126			defer repo.Close()
   127			syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush(ctx, repo, ps)
   128			if !checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook(ctx, repo) {
   129				// Policy failures should skip checkpoint pushes, not abort the user's push.
   130				return nil
   131			}
   132		}
   133	
   134		// OPF pre-push rewrite: if OPF is configured, resolve the user's
   135		// decision (env > settings > prompt > non-TTY auto-run), then
   136		// re-redact unpushed v1 commits with OPF (producing the OPF-applied,
   137		// 9-layer pipeline) before pushing. Skipped entirely when OPF is off,
   138		// so the common-case fast path is unchanged.
   139		if redact.OPFEnabled() {
   140			decision, decisionErr := opfPrePushDecision(ctx)
   141			if decisionErr != nil {
   142				logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF pre-push decision failed; aborting push",
   143					slog.String("error", decisionErr.Error()),
   144				)
   145				return decisionErr
   146			}
   147			switch decision {
   148			case OPFAbort:
   149				return errOPFAbortedByUser
   150			case OPFSkip:
   151				// User opted out for this push (or settings/env say
   152				// "never"). Push regex-only (8-layer) content as-is.
   153				logging.Info(ctx, "OPF skipped for this push (user choice or settings)")
   154			case OPFRun:
   155				_, opfSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "opf_pre_push_rewrite")
   156				if repoErr != nil {
   157					opfSpan.RecordError(repoErr)
   158					opfSpan.End()
   159					logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF pre-push: failed to open repo; aborting push",
   160						slog.String("error", repoErr.Error()),
   161					)
   162					return repoErr
   163				}
   164				if _, rewriteErr := RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF(ctx, repo, ps.pushTarget()); rewriteErr != nil {
   165					opfSpan.RecordError(rewriteErr)
   166					opfSpan.End()
   167					logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF pre-push rewrite failed; aborting push",
   168						slog.String("error", rewriteErr.Error()),
   169					)
   170					return rewriteErr
   171				}
   172				opfSpan.End()
   173			}
   174		}
   175	
   176		if deferAutomaticCheckpointPush {
   177			// Do this only after OPF has had a chance to rewrite v1: the outer
   178			// user push may explicitly include the metadata branch.
   179			logging.Info(ctx, "automatic checkpoint push deferred until the remote has a branch",
   180				slog.String("remote", ps.remote),
   181			)
   182			return nil
   183		}
   184	
   185		// Thread the span's context into the push so the network push and any
   186		// fetch+rebase recovery nest beneath it as child steps in the perf trace.
   187		pushCtx, pushCheckpointsSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_checkpoint_refs")
   188		// Capture needs checkpoint data CONFIRMED on this remote, so count what
   189		// landed rather than trusting the absence of an error: every ref that was due
   190		// has to deliver, and at least one has to actually do so. Delivery must come
   191		// from pushRefIfNeeded's delivered return and NOT from err, which is
   192		// fail-soft and nil even when the remote refused the ref.
   193		deliveredCount, anyFailed := 0, false
   194		for _, ref := range refs.Push {
   195			delivered, err := pushRefIfNeeded(pushCtx, ps.pushTarget(), ref)
   196			if err != nil {
   197				pushCheckpointsSpan.RecordError(err)
   198				pushCheckpointsSpan.End()
   199				return err
   200			}
   201			if delivered {
   202				deliveredCount++
   203			} else {
   204				anyFailed = true
   205			}
   206		}
   207		pushCheckpointsSpan.End()
   208	
   209		// Delivered: the election may now follow the push that carried it. A push that
   210		// carried nothing — an empty ref set, or a v1 ref that does not exist locally
   211		// yet — leaves the election alone. It is safe either way (nothing is stranded
   212		// when there was nothing to strand), but capturing would announce a move that
   213		// moved no data, which is the class of claim this whole path exists to stop
   214		// making. The next push that carries a checkpoint captures instead.
   215		if pendingCapture != "" && deliveredCount > 0 && !anyFailed {
   216			commitCapturedSyncRemote(ctx, pendingCapture)
   217		}
   218	
   219		cleanupPushedShadowBranches(ctx)
   220		return nil
   221	}

   223	// opfPrePushDecision resolves the user's OPF decision for this push (env >
   224	// settings > prompt > non-TTY auto-run). Shared by both checkpoint backends so
   225	// the precedence cannot drift between them.
   226	func opfPrePushDecision(ctx context.Context) (OPFDecision, error) {
   227		cfg, _ := settings.Load(ctx) //nolint:errcheck // Load already failed at hook init; fall back to nil
   228		var opfCfg *settings.OPFSettings
   229		if cfg != nil && cfg.Redaction != nil {
   230			opfCfg = cfg.Redaction.OpenAIPrivacyFilter
   231		}
   232		return resolveOPFDecisionForPrePush(ctx, opfCfg, opfPrePushProgressWriter)
   233	}
   234	
   235	// runOPFForCheckpointRefs resolves the OPF decision and, when it says run,
   236	// rewrites the queued checkpoint refs. It reports whether the flush may
   237	// proceed: false means OPF failed or the user aborted, so the caller withholds
   238	// the checkpoint push and leaves the refs queued.
   239	func runOPFForCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository) bool {
   240		decision, err := opfPrePushDecision(ctx)
   241		if err != nil {
   242			warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld(ctx, err)
   243			return false
   244		}
   245		switch decision {
   246		case OPFAbort:
   247			warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld(ctx, errOPFAbortedByUser)
   248			return false
   249		case OPFSkip:
   250			// Explicit opt-out for this push: flush the 8-layer content as-is,
   251			// untagged — same as the v1 path.
   252			logging.Info(ctx, "OPF skipped for this push (user choice or settings)")
   253		case OPFRun:
   254			_, opfSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "opf_pre_push_rewrite_refs")
   255			defer opfSpan.End()
   256			if rewriteErr := RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF(ctx, repo); rewriteErr != nil {
   257				opfSpan.RecordError(rewriteErr)
   258				warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld(ctx, rewriteErr)
   259				return false
   260			}
   261		}
   262		return true
   263	}
   264	
   265	// warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld reports a withheld flush on both channels: the
   266	// log for diagnosis, and the user's terminal so a silently un-synced checkpoint
   267	// is never the first they hear of it.
   268	func warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld(ctx context.Context, err error) {
   269		logging.Warn(ctx, "OPF pre-push failed; skipping checkpoint ref push, refs left queued",
   270			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   271		)
   272		fmt.Fprintf(stderrWriter,
   273			"[entire] OPF did not run, so checkpoint refs were not pushed and stay queued for your next push: %v\n", err)
   274	}
   275	
   276	// deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote reports whether publication of the git-branch
   277	// v1 metadata should be held back because the push remote may be brand new.
   278	//
   279	// Hosting providers such as GitHub make the first branch pushed to an empty
   280	// repository its default, so the pre-push hook must not publish
   281	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ahead of the user's own first branch. The check is
   282	// purely local: if a remote-tracking ref for this remote already exists
   283	// (refs/remotes/<remote>/*), the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   284	// before and therefore already has at least one branch, so publishing cannot
   285	// make our metadata the default. Otherwise defer — git records a
   286	// remote-tracking ref after the first successful push, so the deferred metadata
   287	// publishes on the next push.
   288	//
   289	// It deliberately performs no ls-remote/fetch. A network round trip on the
   290	// pre-push path can trigger an SSH security-key touch prompt (and doing so per
   291	// push URL would multiply those prompts), which is a poor pre-push UX. This is
   292	// also why it uses only the remote git handed the hook rather than resolving
   293	// every configured push URL.
   294	//
   295	// A separate checkpoint remote is exempt: it is a dedicated metadata store, not
   296	// the repository the user pushes to.
   297	func deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote(ctx context.Context, ps pushSettings) bool {
   298		if ps.hasCheckpointURL() {
   299			return false
   300		}
   301	
   302		// The hazard only arises for a configured remote (the `git remote add
   303		// origin …` then first-push flow). Pushing straight to a bare URL hands that
   304		// URL to the hook as the remote arg, and git never records a
   305		// refs/remotes/<url>/* tracking ref for it — so a tracking-ref check would
   306		// defer the metadata forever. Publish for a non-configured (URL) target
   307		// rather than strand it; the first-branch scenario always uses a named
   308		// remote.
   309		if !isConfiguredRemote(ctx, ps.remote) {
   310			return false
   311		}
   312	
   313		// Known limitation, accepted for the no-network design: a tracking ref left
   314		// over from before a remote was deleted and recreated empty under the same
   315		// URL reads as "established", so v1 would publish to the now-empty remote.
   316		// Detecting that requires asking the remote — the network round trip we
   317		// deliberately avoid here. The scenario is rare and its default branch is
   318		// recoverable by resetting it on the forge.
   319		return !remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx, ps.remote)
   320	}
   321	
   322	// isConfiguredRemote reports whether name is a configured git remote, as
   323	// opposed to a bare URL that git passes through verbatim when a push targets a
   324	// URL directly. Local and best-effort (reads config, no network); any error is
   325	// treated as "not a configured remote".
   326	func isConfiguredRemote(ctx context.Context, name string) bool {
   327		if name == "" {
   328			return false
   329		}
   330		return cachedIsConfiguredRemote(ctx, name, func() (bool, error) {
   331			cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", name)
   332			if worktreeRoot, ok := settings.WorktreeRoot(ctx); ok {
   333				cmd.Dir = worktreeRoot
   334			}
   335			err := cmd.Run()
   336			if err == nil {
   337				return true, nil
   338			}
   339			// git ran and said no: a real answer worth caching. git failing to run at
   340			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   340			// all says nothing about the remote, and memoizing that false would
   341			// fail-close checkpoint_push_remote for the rest of the process.
   342			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   343			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   344				return false, nil
   345			}
   346			return false, fmt.Errorf("probe remote %q: %w", name, err)
   347		})
   348	}
   349	
   350	// remoteHasTrackingRefs reports whether any refs/remotes/<remote>/* ref exists
   351	// locally. Its presence means the remote has been fetched from or pushed to
   352	// before and so already has at least one branch. Local-only and best-effort:
   353	// any error is treated as "no tracking refs" so the caller fails safe (defers).
   354	func remoteHasTrackingRefs(ctx context.Context, remote string) bool {
   355		if remote == "" {
   356			return false
   357		}
   358		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "for-each-ref", "--count=1", "refs/remotes/"+remote+"/")
   359		out, err := cmd.Output()
   360		if err != nil {
   361			return false
   362		}
   363		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)) != ""
   364	}
   365	
   366	// prePushCheckpointRefs drains the per-checkpoint push queue and batch-pushes the
   367	// recorded refs fast-forward-only (git-refs primary; never a force push — a
   368	// diverged ref is recovered via fetch+replay). Transient push failures are logged and
   369	// swallowed — like the v1 path, they must not block the user's git push — and the
   370	// refs stay queued for the next pre-push. When OPF is enabled the queued refs
   371	// are re-redacted with it first (RewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF).
   372	//
   373	// It honors the checkpoint policy exactly like the v1 path: the policy gates on
   374	// checkpoint *format* compatibility (diverged from the remote, or an unsupported
   375	// local format), which is independent of the storage backend, so a blocked
   376	// policy skips the ref push (leaving refs queued) rather than pushing.
   377	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) prePushCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, ps pushSettings, pendingCapture string) error {
   378		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
   379		if err != nil {
   380			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: open repo failed; skipping checkpoint push",
   381				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   382			return nil
   383		}
   384		defer repo.Close()
   385	
   386		// Refresh the checkpoint policy from the remote, then skip the ref push
   387		// (leaving refs queued) if the policy is diverged or the local format is
   388		// unsupported — same gate the v1 path uses.
   389		syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush(ctx, repo, ps)
   390		if !checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook(ctx, repo) {
   391			return nil
   392		}
   393	
   394		// OPF backend divergence: both paths fail closed, but this one does it
   395		// without blocking the user. The v1 path aborts the user's git push; here a
   396		// checkpoint-ref failure must never do that (see this function's doc), so
   397		// failing closed means withholding the flush — nothing un-OPF'd ships, the
   398		// refs stay queued, and the user's push proceeds.
   399		if redact.OPFEnabled() && !runOPFForCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo) {
   400			return nil
   401		}
   402	
   403		if flushed, err := flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repo, ps); err == nil {
   404			// Delivered, and only if something actually was: an empty queue pushed
   405			// nothing, so it must not move the election or announce that it had.
   406			if pendingCapture != "" && flushed > 0 {
   407				commitCapturedSyncRemote(ctx, pendingCapture)
   408			}
   409		} else {
   410			// Fail-soft: a checkpoint-ref push failure must never block the user's
   411			// git push. The refs stay queued for the next pre-push.
   412			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: checkpoint ref push failed; refs left queued",
   413				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   414		}
   415	
   416		cleanupPushedShadowBranches(ctx)
   417		return nil
   418	}
   419	
   420	// PushQueuedCheckpointRefs pushes any queued checkpoint refs to the configured
   421	// checkpoint remote, surfacing errors (unlike the fail-soft pre-push path); the
   422	// caller owns the repo. It returns the number of refs pushed and whether
   423	// pushing is disabled in settings — a distinct signal from pushed==0 with
   424	// pushing enabled (an empty queue), so callers can report the two accurately.
   425	// Like the pre-push paths, a checkpoint policy that blocks pushing errors with
   426	// the refs left queued. Currently used by the checkpoint migration command's
   427	// opt-in "push now".
   428	func PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, remote string) (pushed int, pushDisabled bool, err error) {
   429		ps := resolvePushSettings(ctx, remote)
   430		if ps.pushDisabled {
   431			return 0, true, nil
   432		}
   433		syncCheckpointPolicyForPrePush(ctx, repo, ps)
   434		if !checkpointPolicyAllowsGitHook(ctx, repo) {
   435			return 0, false, errors.New("checkpoint policy does not allow pushing checkpoint refs; refs stay queued")
   436		}
   437		pushed, err = flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx, repo, ps)
   438		// Clean up even on a partial/failed flush: a diverged batch can push some
   439		// refs and still return an error, and the shadow branches for the refs that
   440		// *did* land must still be cleaned up — parity with the pre-push path, which
   441		// always runs cleanup after flush regardless of its error.
   442		cleanupPushedShadowBranches(ctx)
   443		return pushed, false, err
   444	}
   445	
   446	// flushCheckpointRefsQueue drains the push-discovery queue and batch-pushes the
   447	// recorded refs fast-forward-only, recovering a diverged ref by fetch+replay and
   448	// removing from the queue only the refs that land. It returns the number pushed.
   449	//
   450	// Shared by the git-refs pre-push path (which logs and ignores the error to
   451	// never block the user's push) and the migration command's opt-in push (which
   452	// surfaces it). Stale entries — refs no longer present locally — are pruned so
   453	// they don't block the queue forever.
   454	func flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ps pushSettings) (int, error) {
   455		queue, err := checkpoint.PushQueueForRepo(ctx, repo)
   456		if err != nil {
   457			return 0, fmt.Errorf("resolve push queue: %w", err)
   458		}
   459		queued, err := queue.Drain()
   460		if err != nil {
   461			return 0, fmt.Errorf("drain push queue: %w", err)
   462		}
   463		if len(queued) == 0 {
   464			return 0, nil
   465		}
   466	
   467		pushCtx, pushSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_checkpoint_refs")
   468		defer pushSpan.End()
   469	
   470		existing, stale := partitionLocalRefs(repo, queued)
   471		if len(stale) > 0 {
   472			if err := queue.Remove(stale); err != nil {
   473				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: prune stale queue entries failed",
   474					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   475			}
   476		}
   477		if len(existing) == 0 {
   478			return 0, nil
   479		}
   480	
   481		// Resolved here, not by the caller: it spawns `git remote get-url` and its
   482		// result is unused unless refs are actually pushed, so an ordinary push with
   483		// an empty queue must not pay for it — nor print the multi-URL warning.
   484		dest := resolveRefsPushDestination(pushCtx, ps)
   485		dest.warnIgnoredPushURLs(pushCtx)
   486	
   487		// Progress: pushing many refs over the network can take tens of seconds, so
   488		// surface it (matching the v1 path's "[entire] Pushing ..." line) instead of
   489		// leaving the user's git push apparently hung. Written to stderr, which git
   490		// shows during the pre-push hook.
   491		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Pushing %d checkpoint ref(s) to %s...", len(existing), dest.display())
   492		stop := startProgressDots(os.Stderr)
   493	
   494		// Fast path: push all refs in one round-trip (fast-forward-only). If every
   495		// ref was up to date or fast-forwarded, we're done.
   496		batchErr := batchPushRefs(pushCtx, dest.target, existing)
   497		if batchErr == nil {
   498			stop(" done")
   499			if removeErr := queue.Remove(existing); removeErr != nil {
   500				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: clear pushed refs from queue failed",
   501					slog.String("error", removeErr.Error()))
   502			}
   503			return len(existing), nil
   504		}
   505		stop("")
   506	
   507		// Non-interactive SSH auth failures cannot be fixed by per-ref
   508		// fetch+replay. Surface the same actionable hint as the v1 doPushRef path
   509		// (issue #1523) instead of only logging to .entire/logs/.
   510		if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(pushCtx, batchErr) {
   511			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: couldn't push checkpoint refs: %v\n", batchErr)
   512			printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
   513			if dest.checkpointRemote {
   514				printCheckpointRemoteHint(dest.target)
   515			}
   516			return 0, batchErr
   517		}
   518	
   519		// At least one ref was rejected — typically a non-fast-forward divergence
   520		// (the same checkpoint re-written on another machine). Retry per ref with
   521		// fetch+replay recovery, and remove from the queue only the refs that land
   522		// (a genuine cherry-pick conflict leaves that ref queued for a later push,
   523		// never force-overwriting the remote).
   524		// Deliberately names no cause: the batch fails on divergence, but just as
   525		// often on an unreachable or unauthorized destination. Telling a user with a
   526		// dead remote that their refs "diverged" — or were "rejected", which equally
   527		// implies the remote answered — sends them after the wrong problem.
   528		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Checkpoint ref push failed; retrying %d ref(s) individually...", len(existing))
   529		stop = startProgressDots(os.Stderr)
   530		pushed := make([]plumbing.ReferenceName, 0, len(existing))
   531		var firstErr error
   532		for _, ref := range existing {
   533			if err := pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(pushCtx, dest.target, ref); err != nil {
   534				logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: checkpoint ref push/sync failed; left queued, not overwritten",
   535					slog.String("ref", ref.String()), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   536				if nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure(pushCtx, err) {
   537					printNonInteractiveSSHAuthHint()
   538				}
   539				if firstErr == nil {
   540					firstErr = err
   541				}
   542				continue
   543			}
   544			pushed = append(pushed, ref)
   545		}
   546		stop(fmt.Sprintf(" pushed %d of %d", len(pushed), len(existing)))
   547		if err := queue.Remove(pushed); err != nil {
   548			logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs push: clear pushed refs from queue failed",
   549				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   550		}
   551		if firstErr != nil {

   276	// deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote reports whether publication of the git-branch

   398		// refs stay queued, and the user's push proceeds.

   408			}

   411			// git push. The refs stay queued for the next pre-push.

   418	}

   454	func flushCheckpointRefsQueue(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ps pushSettings) (int, error) {

   458		}

   461			return 0, fmt.Errorf("drain push queue: %w", err)
   462		}

   464			return 0, nil

   467		pushCtx, pushSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "push_checkpoint_refs")

   726	// uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket all do).
   727	//
   728	// The fetch targets come from checkpointBlobFetchTargets: the single dedicated
   729	// checkpoint_remote URL when one is configured, otherwise one target per
   730	// checkpoint read candidate, tried in order (first success wins; blob fetches
   731	// land in the object store, never in local refs, so both tiers are legal).
   732	//
   733	// If fetching by hash fails on every target, falls back to a full metadata
   734	// branch fetch.
   735	func FetchBlobsByHash(ctx context.Context, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {
   736		return fetchBlobsByHash(ctx, hashes, remote.ReadFetchTimeout, remote.ReadChainBudget, remote.FetchBlobs)
   737	}
   738	
   739	func fetchBlobsByHash(
   740		ctx context.Context,
   741		hashes []plumbing.Hash,
   742		fetchTimeout time.Duration,
   743		chainBudget time.Duration,
   744		fetchBlobs func(context.Context, string, []string) error,
   745	) error {
   746		if len(hashes) == 0 {
   747			return nil
   748		}
   749	
   750		// One ceiling over the whole operation — the per-target loop AND the
   751		// fallback fetches below. Before the read-candidate chain this function was
   752		// wrapped in a single 2-minute budget that covered its fallbacks; moving to
   753		// per-target budgets dropped that, leaving the fallbacks on the caller's
   754		// uncapped context, so a fully-stalled hydration could run per-target
   755		// budgets and then a fresh per-candidate metadata chain on top.
   756		ctx, cancelChain := context.WithTimeout(ctx, chainBudget)
   757		defer cancelChain()
   758	
   759		// The loop is bounded below the ceiling so a fully-stalled set of targets
   760		// cannot spend the fallbacks' window too — "covered by the ceiling" has to
   761		// mean funded, not merely inside it.
   762		loopCtx, cancelLoop := context.WithTimeout(ctx, remote.ReadChainLoopBudget(chainBudget))
   763		defer cancelLoop()
   764	
   765		targets := checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx)
   766	
   767		hashStrs := make([]string, len(hashes))
   768		for i, h := range hashes {
   769			hashStrs[i] = h.String()
   770		}
   771	
   772		var firstErr error
   773		for i, fetchTarget := range targets {
   774			candidateCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, fetchTimeout)
   775			fetchErr := fetchBlobs(candidateCtx, fetchTarget, hashStrs)
   776			cancel()
   777			if fetchErr == nil {
   778				return nil
   779			}
   780			if firstErr == nil {
   781				firstErr = fetchErr
   782			}
   783			logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed on target",
   784				slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   785				slog.String("fetch_target", remote.RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget)),
   786				slog.Int("target_index", i),
   787				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
   788			)
   789		}
   790	
   791		logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed, falling back to full metadata fetch",
   792			slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   793			slog.String("error", firstErr.Error()),
   794		)
   795		// Fallback: try checkpoint remote first (if configured), then the
   796		// read-candidate chain.
   797		if cpErr := FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote(ctx); cpErr != nil {
   798			if fallbackErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fallbackErr != nil {
   799				return fmt.Errorf("fetch-by-hash failed: %w; fallback fetch also failed: %w",
   800					firstErr, fallbackErr)
   801			}
   802		}
   803	
   804		return nil
   805	}
   806	
   807	// checkpointBlobFetchTargets returns the ordered fetch targets for blob
   808	// hydration. A configured checkpoint_remote is a dedicated store with a single
   809	// authoritative target; otherwise each checkpoint read candidate becomes a
   810	// target (its URL when resolvable — reusing the checkpoint-token URL
   811	// derivation — else the bare remote name). An empty candidate chain keeps the
   812	// legacy single-target shape so error reporting matches today's remoteless
   813	// behavior.
   814	func checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx context.Context) []string {
   815		if remote.Configured(ctx) {
   816			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   817		}
   818		candidates := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx)
   819		if len(candidates) == 0 {
   820			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   821		}
   822		targets := make([]string, 0, len(candidates))
   823		for _, name := range candidates {
   824			targets = append(targets, remote.CheckpointFetchTargetFrom(ctx, name))
   825		}
   826		return targets
   827	}

   360	// metadataFetchDepth is the absolute --depth used when fetching the metadata

   365	const metadataFetchDepth = 1_000_000_000
   366	
   367	// FetchMetadataBranch fetches the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch from the

   375	// FetchMetadataTreeOnly fetches the entire/checkpoints/v1 commit+tree graph
   376	// from the checkpoint read-candidate remotes to resolve the latest
   377	// checkpoint, relying on --filter=blob:none (when filtered fetches are
   378	// enabled) to skip blob content rather than on a shallow --depth=1 fetch.
   379	//
   380	// It deliberately does NOT use --depth=1. A depth-1 fetch adds the fetched tip
   381	// to .git/shallow, and any ref pointing at a shallow commit (the durable
   382	// refs/remotes/origin/<branch> that git updates opportunistically, or the local
   383	// primary) can no longer be walked past that boundary. A later `git merge-base`
   384	// against it then falsely reports "no common ancestor", which makes push and
   385	// `entire doctor` treat an ordinary diverged-but-behind branch as disconnected
   386	// (see strategy.IsMetadataDisconnected). Fetching at full depth keeps the
   387	// remote-tracking ref connected; git fetches incrementally, so after the first
   388	// fetch only new commits/trees travel.
   389	//
   390	// It also heals a repo that an older CLI already shallowed: the ref-scoped deep
   391	// fetch removes the boundary left by a prior --depth=1 fetch rather than letting
   392	// it linger forever, without deepening an independently-shallow source tree.
   393	func FetchMetadataTreeOnly(ctx context.Context) error {

   396	
   397	// fetchMetadataFromReadRemotes fetches the metadata branch from every checkpoint
   398	// read candidate. A successful branch fetch does not prove that branch contains
   399	// the checkpoint a caller will request, so stopping at the first existing branch
   400	// would let partial elected-remote history hide legacy origin data. Candidate
   401	// failures are logged; the operation succeeds when any candidate was fetched,
   402	// and surfaces the first error only when every candidate fails.
   403	//
   404	// Local-ref advancement is confined to the elected checkpoint sync remote: a
   405	// successful fetch from the legacy origin tier only updates origin's tracking
   406	// ref (which the candidate-aware tracking-ref readers consult) and never feeds
   407	// SafelyAdvanceLocalRef — a stale origin driving the local v1 advance is the
   408	// #1374-class hazard. The election result comes from the same resolver call
   409	// that produced the chain (never inferred from the chain's first entry, which
   410	// can be the fail-open origin), so chain and election cannot disagree
   411	// mid-operation.
   412	func fetchMetadataFromReadRemotes(ctx context.Context, noFilter bool) error {
   413		resolution := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection(ctx)
   414		candidates := resolution.Candidates
   415		if len(candidates) == 0 {
   416			return errors.New("no git remotes configured to fetch checkpoint metadata from")
   417		}
   418	
   419		// Per-candidate budgets (inside fetchMetadataFromRemote) nested in one chain
   420		// ceiling, so a stalled candidate cannot starve the rest and the total stays
   421		// bounded — these read paths have no outer deadline above them.
   422		chainCtx, cancelChain := remote.WithReadChainBudget(ctx)
   423		defer cancelChain()
   424	
   425		var firstErr error
   426		fetched := false
   427		for i, remoteName := range candidates {
   428			// After one successful fetch, later (legacy) candidates are fetched
   429			// only to BOOTSTRAP a missing tracking ref — a fresh clone needs
   430			// origin's legacy tier once for the union readers, but re-fetching an
   431			// already-present legacy tier on every resume doubles the deep-fetch
   432			// cost for data that writes no longer land on. Content availability
   433			// is preserved: the union readers consult the existing tracking ref.
   434			// The trade-off: a mixed-version teammate still pushing v1 to origin
   435			// refreshes here only when the elected fetch fails or the tracking
   436			// ref is absent.
   437			if fetched && metadataTrackingRefExists(ctx, remoteName) {
   438				logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata branch fetch: skipping already-present legacy candidate",
   439					slog.String("candidate", remoteName))
   440				continue
   441			}
   442			err := fetchMetadataFromRemote(chainCtx, remoteName, noFilter, resolution.ElectedName != "" && remoteName == resolution.ElectedName)
   443			if err == nil {
   444				fetched = true
   445				continue
   446			}
   447			if firstErr == nil {
   448				firstErr = err
   449			}
   450			logging.Debug(ctx, "metadata branch fetch: read candidate failed",
   451				slog.String("candidate", remoteName),
   452				slog.Int("candidate_index", i),
   453				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   454		}

   457		}
   458		return firstErr
   459	}

   588	// checkpointRefListTimeout bounds the names-only ls-remote used by user-facing

   595	// ListCheckpointRefsOnRemote enumerates the per-checkpoint refs

   642			}

   644			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, candidateTimeout)

   647			output, err := remote.LsRemoteInDir(ctx, worktreeRoot, url, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix+"*")

   650			}

   657		candidates := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx)
   658		if len(candidates) == 0 {

   660		}

   662		seen := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]bool)
   663		var names []plumbing.ReferenceName
   664		var firstErr error
   665		succeeded := false
   666		for _, candidate := range candidates {
   667			candidateCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, candidateTimeout)
   668			// Prefer the candidate's resolved URL (token-aware, worktree-pinned);
   669			// fall back to the bare remote name, which git resolves itself.
   670			target := candidate
   671			if url, urlErr := remote.FetchURL(candidateCtx, remote.FetchURLOptions{WorktreeRoot: worktreeRoot, LeadReadRemote: candidate}); urlErr == nil {
   672				target = url
   673			}
   674			output, lsErr := remote.LsRemoteInDir(candidateCtx, worktreeRoot, target, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix+"*")
   675			cancel()
   676			if lsErr != nil {

   678					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("ls-remote checkpoint refs from %s: %w", remote.RedactURLOrPath(target), lsErr)
   679				}
   680				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint ref discovery: read candidate listing failed; continuing with remaining candidates",
   681					slog.String("candidate", candidate),
   682					slog.String("error", lsErr.Error()))
   683				continue
   684			}
   685			succeeded = true
   686			for _, name := range parseCheckpointRefNames(output) {
   687				if seen[name] {
   688					continue
   689				}
   690				seen[name] = true
   691				names = append(names, name)
   692			}
   693		}

   696		}

   700	// parseCheckpointRefNames extracts the checkpoint ref names from `git ls-remote`
   701	// output. Each line is "<hash>\t<refname>"; only refs under CheckpointRefPrefix
   702	// are kept (the store re-validates each via ParseRef). Checkpoint refs point at
   703	// commits so no peeled (`^{}`) lines appear for them; refs/tags peeled lines
   704	// lack the checkpoint prefix and drop out here; any anomalous
   705	// refs/entire/checkpoints/...^{} name is rejected by ParseRef downstream (the
   706	// "{}" shard never matches ShardFor).
   707	func parseCheckpointRefNames(output []byte) []plumbing.ReferenceName {
   708		var names []plumbing.ReferenceName
   709		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
   710			fields := strings.Fields(line)
   711			if len(fields) < 2 {
   712				continue
   713			}
   714			name := fields[1]
   715			if !strings.HasPrefix(name, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix) {
   716				continue
   717			}
   718			names = append(names, plumbing.ReferenceName(name))
   719		}
   720		return names

   723	// FetchBlobsByHash fetches specific blob objects from the remote by their SHA-1 hashes.
   724	// Uses "git fetch <target> <hash>" which goes through normal credential helpers,
   725	// unlike fetch-pack which bypasses them. Requires the server to support
   726	// uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket all do).
   727	//
   728	// The fetch targets come from checkpointBlobFetchTargets: the single dedicated
   729	// checkpoint_remote URL when one is configured, otherwise one target per
   730	// checkpoint read candidate, tried in order (first success wins; blob fetches
   731	// land in the object store, never in local refs, so both tiers are legal).
   732	//
   733	// If fetching by hash fails on every target, falls back to a full metadata
   734	// branch fetch.
   735	func FetchBlobsByHash(ctx context.Context, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {

   739	func fetchBlobsByHash(
   740		ctx context.Context,
   741		hashes []plumbing.Hash,
   742		fetchTimeout time.Duration,
   743		chainBudget time.Duration,
   744		fetchBlobs func(context.Context, string, []string) error,
   745	) error {
   746		if len(hashes) == 0 {
   747			return nil
   748		}
   749	
   750		// One ceiling over the whole operation — the per-target loop AND the
   751		// fallback fetches below. Before the read-candidate chain this function was
   752		// wrapped in a single 2-minute budget that covered its fallbacks; moving to
   753		// per-target budgets dropped that, leaving the fallbacks on the caller's
   754		// uncapped context, so a fully-stalled hydration could run per-target
   755		// budgets and then a fresh per-candidate metadata chain on top.
   756		ctx, cancelChain := context.WithTimeout(ctx, chainBudget)
   757		defer cancelChain()
   758	
   759		// The loop is bounded below the ceiling so a fully-stalled set of targets
   760		// cannot spend the fallbacks' window too — "covered by the ceiling" has to
   761		// mean funded, not merely inside it.
   762		loopCtx, cancelLoop := context.WithTimeout(ctx, remote.ReadChainLoopBudget(chainBudget))
   763		defer cancelLoop()
   764	
   765		targets := checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx)
   766	
   767		hashStrs := make([]string, len(hashes))
   768		for i, h := range hashes {
   769			hashStrs[i] = h.String()
   770		}
   771	
   772		var firstErr error
   773		for i, fetchTarget := range targets {
   774			candidateCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, fetchTimeout)
   775			fetchErr := fetchBlobs(candidateCtx, fetchTarget, hashStrs)
   776			cancel()
   777			if fetchErr == nil {
   778				return nil
   779			}
   780			if firstErr == nil {
   781				firstErr = fetchErr
   782			}
   783			logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed on target",
   784				slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   785				slog.String("fetch_target", remote.RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget)),
   786				slog.Int("target_index", i),
   787				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
   788			)
   789		}
   790	
   791		logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed, falling back to full metadata fetch",
   792			slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   793			slog.String("error", firstErr.Error()),
   794		)
   795		// Fallback: try checkpoint remote first (if configured), then the
   796		// read-candidate chain.
   797		if cpErr := FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote(ctx); cpErr != nil {
   798			if fallbackErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fallbackErr != nil {
   799				return fmt.Errorf("fetch-by-hash failed: %w; fallback fetch also failed: %w",
   800					firstErr, fallbackErr)
   801			}
   802		}
   803	
   804		return nil
   805	}
   806	
   807	// checkpointBlobFetchTargets returns the ordered fetch targets for blob
   808	// hydration. A configured checkpoint_remote is a dedicated store with a single
   809	// authoritative target; otherwise each checkpoint read candidate becomes a
   810	// target (its URL when resolvable — reusing the checkpoint-token URL
   811	// derivation — else the bare remote name). An empty candidate chain keeps the
   812	// legacy single-target shape so error reporting matches today's remoteless
   813	// behavior.
   814	func checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx context.Context) []string {
   815		if remote.Configured(ctx) {
   816			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   817		}
   818		candidates := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx)
   819		if len(candidates) == 0 {
   820			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   821		}
   822		targets := make([]string, 0, len(candidates))
   823		for _, name := range candidates {
   824			targets = append(targets, remote.CheckpointFetchTargetFrom(ctx, name))
   825		}
   826		return targets
   827	}

   397	// fetchMetadataFromReadRemotes fetches the metadata branch from every checkpoint

   399	// the checkpoint a caller will request, so stopping at the first existing branch
   400	// would let partial elected-remote history hide legacy origin data. Candidate
   401	// failures are logged; the operation succeeds when any candidate was fetched,
   402	// and surfaces the first error only when every candidate fails.
   403	//
   404	// Local-ref advancement is confined to the elected checkpoint sync remote: a
   405	// successful fetch from the legacy origin tier only updates origin's tracking
   406	// ref (which the candidate-aware tracking-ref readers consult) and never feeds

   408	// #1374-class hazard. The election result comes from the same resolver call
   409	// that produced the chain (never inferred from the chain's first entry, which
   410	// can be the fail-open origin), so chain and election cannot disagree
   411	// mid-operation.
   412	func fetchMetadataFromReadRemotes(ctx context.Context, noFilter bool) error {
   413		resolution := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection(ctx)

   700	// parseCheckpointRefNames extracts the checkpoint ref names from `git ls-remote`

   704	// lack the checkpoint prefix and drop out here; any anomalous
   705	// refs/entire/checkpoints/...^{} name is rejected by ParseRef downstream (the
   706	// "{}" shard never matches ShardFor).
   707	func parseCheckpointRefNames(output []byte) []plumbing.ReferenceName {
   708		var names []plumbing.ReferenceName
   709		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
   710			fields := strings.Fields(line)
   711			if len(fields) < 2 {
   712				continue

   709		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(output), "\n") {
   710			fields := strings.Fields(line)
   711			if len(fields) < 2 {
   712				continue
   713			}
   714			name := fields[1]
   715			if !strings.HasPrefix(name, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix) {
   716				continue
   717			}
   718			names = append(names, plumbing.ReferenceName(name))
   719		}
   720		return names
   721	}
   722	
   723	// FetchBlobsByHash fetches specific blob objects from the remote by their SHA-1 hashes.
   724	// Uses "git fetch <target> <hash>" which goes through normal credential helpers,
   725	// unlike fetch-pack which bypasses them. Requires the server to support
   726	// uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket all do).
   727	//
   728	// The fetch targets come from checkpointBlobFetchTargets: the single dedicated
   729	// checkpoint_remote URL when one is configured, otherwise one target per
   730	// checkpoint read candidate, tried in order (first success wins; blob fetches
   731	// land in the object store, never in local refs, so both tiers are legal).
   732	//
   733	// If fetching by hash fails on every target, falls back to a full metadata
   734	// branch fetch.
   735	func FetchBlobsByHash(ctx context.Context, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {
   736		return fetchBlobsByHash(ctx, hashes, remote.ReadFetchTimeout, remote.ReadChainBudget, remote.FetchBlobs)
   737	}
   738	
   739	func fetchBlobsByHash(
   740		ctx context.Context,
   741		hashes []plumbing.Hash,
   742		fetchTimeout time.Duration,
   743		chainBudget time.Duration,
   744		fetchBlobs func(context.Context, string, []string) error,
   745	) error {
   746		if len(hashes) == 0 {
   747			return nil
   748		}
   749	
   750		// One ceiling over the whole operation — the per-target loop AND the
   751		// fallback fetches below. Before the read-candidate chain this function was
   752		// wrapped in a single 2-minute budget that covered its fallbacks; moving to
   753		// per-target budgets dropped that, leaving the fallbacks on the caller's
   754		// uncapped context, so a fully-stalled hydration could run per-target
   755		// budgets and then a fresh per-candidate metadata chain on top.
   756		ctx, cancelChain := context.WithTimeout(ctx, chainBudget)
   757		defer cancelChain()
   758	
   759		// The loop is bounded below the ceiling so a fully-stalled set of targets
   760		// cannot spend the fallbacks' window too — "covered by the ceiling" has to
   761		// mean funded, not merely inside it.
   762		loopCtx, cancelLoop := context.WithTimeout(ctx, remote.ReadChainLoopBudget(chainBudget))
   763		defer cancelLoop()
   764	
   765		targets := checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx)
   766	
   767		hashStrs := make([]string, len(hashes))
   768		for i, h := range hashes {
   769			hashStrs[i] = h.String()
   770		}
   771	
   772		var firstErr error
   773		for i, fetchTarget := range targets {
   774			candidateCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(loopCtx, fetchTimeout)
   775			fetchErr := fetchBlobs(candidateCtx, fetchTarget, hashStrs)
   776			cancel()
   777			if fetchErr == nil {
   778				return nil
   779			}
   780			if firstErr == nil {
   781				firstErr = fetchErr
   782			}
   783			logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed on target",
   784				slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   785				slog.String("fetch_target", remote.RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget)),
   786				slog.Int("target_index", i),
   787				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
   788			)
   789		}
   790	
   791		logging.Debug(ctx, "fetch-by-hash failed, falling back to full metadata fetch",
   792			slog.Int("blob_count", len(hashes)),
   793			slog.String("error", firstErr.Error()),
   794		)
   795		// Fallback: try checkpoint remote first (if configured), then the
   796		// read-candidate chain.
   797		if cpErr := FetchMetadataFromCheckpointRemote(ctx); cpErr != nil {
   798			if fallbackErr := FetchMetadataBranch(ctx); fallbackErr != nil {
   799				return fmt.Errorf("fetch-by-hash failed: %w; fallback fetch also failed: %w",
   800					firstErr, fallbackErr)
   801			}
   802		}
   803	
   804		return nil
   805	}
   806	
   807	// checkpointBlobFetchTargets returns the ordered fetch targets for blob
   808	// hydration. A configured checkpoint_remote is a dedicated store with a single
   809	// authoritative target; otherwise each checkpoint read candidate becomes a
   810	// target (its URL when resolvable — reusing the checkpoint-token URL
   811	// derivation — else the bare remote name). An empty candidate chain keeps the
   812	// legacy single-target shape so error reporting matches today's remoteless
   813	// behavior.
   814	func checkpointBlobFetchTargets(ctx context.Context) []string {
   815		if remote.Configured(ctx) {
   816			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   817		}
   818		candidates := strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx)
   819		if len(candidates) == 0 {
   820			return []string{resolveCheckpointFetchTarget(ctx)}
   821		}
   822		targets := make([]string, 0, len(candidates))
   823		for _, name := range candidates {
   824			targets = append(targets, remote.CheckpointFetchTargetFrom(ctx, name))
   825		}
   826		return targets
   827	}

83677f7510e7eef5fa64711ac3274eda299d8ea1
Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again

NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
caches and manifests are all reconstructible. It is not free either,
measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload (1.02ms against 71µs) with session
state written on every agent hook. What is surrendered is stated in the
doc rather than left implicit.

Writing atomically into an agent's config directory does leave a temp
file beside the target if the process dies between the create and the
rename. The window is now a few tens of microseconds and only `enable`
and `trail checkout` can open it, but the result is permanent, and
Entire diffs untracked files across a turn — so a months-old
.claude/settings.json.<hex>.tmp gets captured into the next checkpoint
as a file that turn created. `entire clean --all` now sweeps them. The
capture path deliberately does NOT learn to ignore them: the worktree
belongs to the user, and silently dropping a file from their checkpoint
is worse than the stray it would hide.

HookConfigFile now refuses a symlinked leaf as well as a symlinked
parent, reversing an earlier decision in this branch. The reason is
recorded where the policy is: the merge read pulls the link target's
contents into what Entire writes, and the write is a rename, so it
replaces the user's link with a regular file rather than following it.
Both are silent. A deliberately symlinked settings.json still works by
keeping it out of the index, which is what a dotfile workflow does.

331c7b1306ee27ec3531e39af3d26662b91754b7
Refuse what os.Root only confined

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

1eaccf7721ef8bc99b649235ed731c1371cdc417
Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.

Follow the rename through strings, comments, skill and docs

The identifier rename in the previous commit left the prose behind. This
is the prose, plus a handful of comments that described the restore path
#2178 deleted.

User-facing text. `checkpoint list --pending` said "No pending rewind
points found." and "Pending rewind points are created automatically
during active agent sessions."; the --pending flag help and the command's
Long text advertised "shadow-branch rewind points"; the two error paths
said "failed to find rewind points". All now say pending checkpoints.
Two assertions in checkpoint_list_test.go pinned the empty-list string
and are updated with it -- they are the only tests that pin any string
this commit touches, and both are exact-match Contains calls, so nothing
else could have silently drifted.

The first-turn context injection told every agent to leave "(enable,
disable, clean, rewind, auth)" to the user. `entire rewind` has not
existed since #1747, so a third of that warning pointed at nothing.
trail_injection_text_test.go asserts only the prefix "Leave setup and
destructive commands", so it still passes; deprecated_strings_test.go
keeps "entire rewind" on its never-advertise list, which is the one place
the name should survive.

Comments. Three were wrong about mechanisms rather than just names, and
those were checked against the code rather than reworded:

  - gitrepo/status.go named "review, rewind" as the paths that keep the
    unbounded Status walk. The rewind one is gone; the two real callers
    are review_target.go and detectFileChangesUnbounded (`session
    adopt`), and the comment now names both.
  - manual_commit_session.go attributed FindSessionsForCommit and
    ClearSessionState to "the rewind reset command". They are called by
    `entire clean` (clean.go:177) and `entire doctor` (doctor.go:406)
    respectively -- different commands, so they get different comments.
  - common.go's DeleteBranchCLI cited HardResetWithProtection as the
    sibling go-git v5 workaround. That function does not exist anywhere
    in the tree; the real one is CheckoutBranch in git_operations.go, and
    the comment now points there.

The rest are vocabulary: agent.go's ProtectedDirs and the mirrored
comments in checkpoint/, session/state.go, api/checkpoint/metadata.go
(comment only -- nothing exported in api/ is renamed), explain.go,
resume.go, transcript.go and strategy/.

Historical references stay, because they explain why the current shape is
what it is: every `rewind --list` mention in checkpoint_list.go and
checkpoint_group.go (that bridge is the reason the JSON is frozen), the
"former interactive rewind picker" that pendingCheckpointLabel inherited
its format from, and manual_commit_workflow_test.go's note about the
assertions that replaced the rewind observations. Also untouched: every
"rewind" that means moving a git ref backwards (fetch_rewind_protection_test.go,
safely_advance_local_ref_test.go, checkpoint_remote_test.go, the
explain fetch tests) and internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go, whose
rewinding is of HTTP request bodies.

Skill and scripts. The harness verb list-rewind-points is now
list-pending-checkpoints, which is two characters wider than the old
longest verb, so the usage block's description column was re-padded to
match. scripts/test-attribution-e2e.sh only ever echoed the phrase; it
already called `checkpoint list --pending --json`.

Docs. CLAUDE.md's method list and Key Files entries pick up the new
identifiers and file name, and sessions-and-checkpoints.md's "## Rewind"
section is "## Pending Checkpoints" with a sentence defining the term
against condensation rather than against a command that no longer exists.
AGENTS.md is a symlink and untouched.

Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again

NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
caches and manifests are all reconstructible. It is not free either,
measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload (1.02ms against 71µs) with session
state written on every agent hook. What is surrendered is stated in the
doc rather than left implicit.

Writing atomically into an agent's config directory does leave a temp
file beside the target if the process dies between the create and the
rename. The window is now a few tens of microseconds and only `enable`
and `trail checkout` can open it, but the result is permanent, and
Entire diffs untracked files across a turn — so a months-old
.claude/settings.json.<hex>.tmp gets captured into the next checkpoint
as a file that turn created. `entire clean --all` now sweeps them. The
capture path deliberately does NOT learn to ignore them: the worktree
belongs to the user, and silently dropping a file from their checkpoint
is worse than the stray it would hide.

HookConfigFile now refuses a symlinked leaf as well as a symlinked
parent, reversing an earlier decision in this branch. The reason is
recorded where the policy is: the merge read pulls the link target's
contents into what Entire writes, and the write is a rename, so it
replaces the user's link with a regular file rather than following it.
Both are silent. A deliberately symlinked settings.json still works by
keeping it out of the index, which is what a dotfile workflow does.
