Refuse what os.Root only confined

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain
filepath.Join produced silently. worktreedir covers the checkpoint tree
entries rewind restores, which may have been fetched from a remote --
rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.
